title: Bengals 53-man roster prediction: Training camp begins
summary: The long summer is nearing an end, at least as far as football is concerned. The Cincinnati Bengals, along with the rest of the NFL, are preparing to return to work at training camp as the league gears up for the preseason. Over the next couple of weeks, the front office will have to whittle down […]
full_text: Dec 21, 2025; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow (9) talks to his teammates Cincinnati Bengals tight end Mike Gesicki (88), Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Mitchell Tinsley (82) and Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase (1) after a play during the second quarter against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images | Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The long summer is nearing an end, at least as far as football is concerned. The Cincinnati Bengals , along with the rest of the NFL, are preparing to return to work at training camp as the league gears up for the preseason. Over the next couple of weeks, the front office will have to whittle down 90 players to 53. Here’s my prediction of who those 53 players will be as training camp begins. Here are the first four versions: Version 1.0 Version 2.0 Version 3.0 Version 4.0 Quarterback (2) Joe Burrow Joe Flacco Cut: Sean Clifford, Josh Johnson Notes: Unless there’s some catastrophic injury, the two guys on the roster will be Burrow and Flacco. Running Back (3) Chase Brown Samaje Perine Tahj Brooks Cut: Gary Brightwell, Kentrell Bullock, Jamal Haynes, Kendall Milton Notes: I think there’s a very small chance the Bengals could find a running back they like in free agency during camp to add to the three above. However, I also think Zac Taylor and Dan Pitcher are comfortable with Brown, Perine and Brooks. I also expect Brooks’ role to be expanded. Wide Receiver (6) Ja’Marr Chase Tee Higgins Andrei Iosivas Charlie Jones Mitchell Tinsley Kendric Pryor Cut: Xavier Johnson, Dohnte Myers, Jordan Moore, Noah Thomas, Ke’Shawn Williams Notes: Chase and Higgins are the best WR duo in the league. Higgins would be WR1 on almost any other team; he happens to be teammates with the best wide receiver in the world. After them, though, there’s a considerable drop. The WR3 job is up for grabs, and could be a revolving door for the Bengals, based on the situation. I do think the Bengals keep six wide receivers and that WR6 job is up for grabs. Chase, Higgins, Iosivas, Jones and Tinsley are locks. Tight End (4) Mike Gesicki Drew Sample Tanner Hudson Erick All Jr. Active/NFI: Josh Kattus Cut: Cam Grandy, Jack Endries Notes: Gesicki is a tight end in name, but plays more like a slot receiver. Sample is used as an extra blocker more often than not, though watching him rumble forward with the ball is always incredible. Hudson has the trust of the coaches, and a healthy All could cut into the playing time of all of the guys ahead of him on the depth chart. I hope the Bengals can keep Endries on the practice squad. Offensive Line (10) Orlando Brown Jr. Dylan Fairchild Ted Karras Dalton Risner Amarius Mims Cody Ford Jalen Rivers Andrew Coker Conner Lew Brian Parker II Cut: OT Javon Foster, OT Corey Robinson II, OT Christian Jones, G Liam Brown, C Jacob Bayer Notes: For the first time in Joe Burrow’s career, he’ll have the same offensive line lined up in front of him for two consecutive seasons. Risner joined the team during training camp last season and fit right in at right guard. Ford is their swing tackle right now. Defensive Line (9) DE Boye Mafe DT Dexter Lawrence II DT Jonathan Allen DE Shemar Stewart DE Myles Murphy DT Kris Jenkins Jr. DT T.J. Slaton Jr. DE Cashius Howell DT Landon Robinson PUP: BJ Hill Cut: DE Isaiah Foskey, DE Cedric Johnson, DT Howard Cross III, DT McKinnley Jackson, DT Jordan Jefferson Notes: Hill starting the season on PUP would have really thrown the Bengals for a loop had it not been for how active they were in free agency. They still have Lawrence and Allen, and Jenkins and Slaton as backups. When Hill returns, I expect he’ll be the 10th defensive lineman, and a cut will come from elsewhere. If Hill gets activated off PUP before final cuts, then things could get really dicey. Do they cut a promising rookie like Landon Robinson? Or does T.J. Slaton become a cap casualty? Linebackers (5) Demetrius Knight Jr. Barrett Carter Oren Burks Joe Giles-Harris Shaka Heyward Cut: Liam Anderson, Swayze Bozeman, Jack Dingle, Eric Gentry, Antwan Powell-Ryland Notes: The linebacker position was BAD in 2025, but both Knight and Carter were rookies, and they had a subpar defensive line in front of them. Now with Lawrence, the most double-teamed nose tackle in the league, occupying linemen, hopefully they’ll both have more space to move and do their jobs. However, if there’s a position where the Bengals could add a free agent during camp where they’d immediately make an impact, it’s at linebacker. Cornerback (6) DJ Turner II Dax Hill Jalen Davis Josh Newton Ja’Sir Taylor Tacario Davis Cut: Jalen Kimber, Bralyn Lux, Ceyair Wright Notes: The only other position I would have liked to see the Bengals add a free agent or a draft pick is at corner. I like Turner and Hill as the team’s two outside corners, and I think Davis can be a solid slot corner. The issue is depth at the position. If there’s an injury, and there often is, I feel like their lack of depth could be a problem. This is the other position I could see the Bengals adding a free agent during camp, especially if someone with a little experience is available. Safety (5) Bryan Cook Jordan Battle Kyle Dugger PJ Jules Daijahn Anthony Cut: Russ Yeast, Isaiah Nwokobia Notes: Cook’s signing was overshadowed by the team’s trade for Lawrence, but his addition could have just as much of an impact. The Bengals have struggled at safety since Jessie Bates left in free agency, but Cook, Battle and Dugger represent the best three they’ve had on the roster since the days of Bates and Vonn Bell. Special Teams (3) K – Evan McPherson P – Ryan Rehkow LS – William Wagner Cut: None Notes: No notes. What do you think? Sound off.

title: Tee Higgins nearly earns the top spot in best WR2 rankings
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals have had one of the best, if not the best, WR2 in Tee Higgins across the NFL since Ja’Marr Chase was drafted back in 2021. Higgins has been regarded as a WR1 and WR1b on the Bengals for years, especially during his contract extension disputes, and has produced impressive numbers despite multiple […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals have had one of the best, if not the best, WR2 in Tee Higgins across the NFL since Ja’Marr Chase was drafted back in 2021. Higgins has been regarded as a WR1 and WR1b on the Bengals for years, especially during his contract extension disputes, and has produced impressive numbers despite multiple injuries. However, heading into 2026, Sports Illustrated has a new name on top of the best WR2 list , and Higgins enters at number 2. “The perfect complement to Ja’Marr Chase, Higgins and Chase have formed the most consistent and highest-paid receiving duo in the league over the past five years. Since joining the Bengals as a second-round pick in 2020, Higgins has recorded two 1,000-yard receiving seasons and two double-digit receiving touchdown seasons. Had Higgins not missed multiple games due to injury in each of the past three seasons, he’d likely have even more 1,000-yard campaigns on his résumé,” SI wrote. “With Higgins and Chase out wide, the Bengals hold one of the best passing attacks in the NFL—especially when Joe Burrow is healthy—and Higgins is a pivotal part of that success as he hauls in contested catches and touchdowns. After all, there’s a reason Burrow vouched so heavily for both Higgins and Chase to get paid,“ SI continued. Higgins has officially been surpassed by Dallas Cowboys wideout George Pickens, who plays alongside their WR1 Ceedee Lamb. Sports Illustrated wrote that the Cowboys have two true WR1’s and Pickens could have an even bigger year in 2026 as he looks to solidify a contract extension in Dallas. No matter what, Higgins is one of the best wideouts in the league and is the perfect complement to Chase when healthy. If Higgins can put together a complete season in 2026, the numbers will show why I believe he is the best of the best.

title: Analytics gives Browns worst playoff chances, by a lot; Cardinals not even listed
summary: Veterans report to Berea, Ohio, on Tuesday for the start of Cleveland Browns training camp. There are still a lot of unknowns, including whether the Browns roster full of young talent will translate to victories, who will start at quarterback, what is next for Dawand Jones, and who will fill out the last two starting […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OH - OCTOBER 16: Chief strategy officer Paul DePodesta (L) and general manager Andrew Berry of the Cleveland Browns watch warmups prior to a game against the New England Patriots at FirstEnergy Stadium on October 16, 2022 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images Veterans report to Berea, Ohio, on Tuesday for the start of Cleveland Browns training camp. There are still a lot of unknowns, including whether the Browns roster full of young talent will translate to victories , who will start at quarterback , what is next for Dawand Jones , and who will fill out the last two starting offensive line spots . Before we get answers to all of that, we are looking forward to training camp highlights and who the camp hero fighting for a roster spot will be for Cleveland this year. As of now, betting line predictions for the Browns are very low . With a new head coach, Myles Garrett out in Los Angeles (and cutting another tie to Cleveland), and another QB competition , there are a lot of reasons to be down on the Browns win total this year… … but this low? So you're telling me there's a chance 😬 pic.twitter.com/GKo601L05m — FTN (@FTNFantasy) July 14, 2026 A little bit about DVOA, an analytical tool I use every year for national playoff prediction pieces for SB Nation : FTN’s DVOA is a metric that breaks down the quality of play compared to the league average while adjusting for the strength of the opponents being played. DVOA is one of a couple of catch-all analytics measures that help us understand the beautiful game of football better. In their playoff prediction data, Cleveland is ranked worse than they were at the end of last year, based on DVOA, when they were 30th in the NFL, ahead of the Las Vegas Raiders and New York Jets. Compared to the DVOA model, FanDuel has the Browns at +700 to make the playoffs , better than three teams, including the Arizona Cardinals, who are a league-worst +2000. As seen above, the Cardinals don’t even make the list, and Cleveland’s odds are half that of any other team. A wide gap between what the analytics data says and what a major sports betting book has the odds. How many teams do you think the Browns should be ahead of in playoff projections? title: Jerry Jeudy video “drama” a preview of Browns training camp QB competition silliness
summary: For those of us of a certain age, “TNT knows drama” was a well-known saying. It often got used in pop culture sayings, at least for a short amount of time, when people were being dramatic. When it comes to the Cleveland Browns quarterback competition, it has all the makings of being “TNT”, both in […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - DECEMBER 07: Shedeur Sanders #12 and Jerry Jeudy #3 of the Cleveland Browns celebrate a 7-yard touchdown pass by Sanders during the fourth quarter against the Tennessee Titans at Huntington Bank Field on December 07, 2025 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images For those of us of a certain age, “TNT knows drama” was a well-known saying. It often got used in pop culture sayings, at least for a short amount of time, when people were being dramatic. When it comes to the Cleveland Browns quarterback competition , it has all the makings of being “TNT”, both in terms of being capable of being explosive but also capable of a lot of drama. Let’s look at the variables: Most important position on the football field A big name, hugely popular QB in Shedeur Sanders A controversial, used-to-be-good QB trying to make an unlikely comeback in Deshaun Watson A team with a long history of struggles at the position A head coach unfraid to speak his mind A team with low expectations and no other national-level storylines That is a crockpot ready for drama and, potentially, very volatile drama. We got our first glimpse of that possibility when Browns WR Jerry Jeudy was live on social media when he was asked who should be Cleveland’s starting quarterback. As noted on ESPN’s lead story , as of Monday morning’s headlines, the clip seems to indicate the receiver wants Watson , but the video looks altered: In the TikTok video , Jeudy flashes four fingers on a livestream, which has been taken by many as a reference to Deshaun Watson, who wears the No. 4. However, the video appears to have been edited as there is a skip in the clip between when Jeudy shows his fingers and when the question is shown. “Yall cut the clip perfectly for that narrative,” Jeudy posted to X on Sunday. The clip in question: Someone asked Jerry Jeudy on Tik Tok who he wants the Browns starting QB to be 👀👀👀👀 pic.twitter.com/dLHykNWv3o — ESPN Cleveland (@ESPNCleveland) July 26, 2026 Anyone watching can clearly see a skip in the video around the four-second mark. Jeudy was unhappy, to say the least: I don’t speak on decisions that aren’t mine to make. I support my teammates/Brothers, I do my job, and control what I can control. Let’s stop creating narrative that aren’t there for likes and clicks. I bet this won’t go viral because it’s too positive/real for y’all 💯. — Jerry Jeudy⁴ (@jerryjeudy) July 26, 2026 Given all the combustible variables noted above, the “drama” surrounding the Jeudy video could be a preview of what is to come during Browns training camp. We’ve all gotten used to the QB tracker; this year we might get some version of a body language tracker as well. Once upon a time, TNT knew drama. As Cleveland Browns training camp opens up, it will be interesting to see if the Jeudy video is truly just a preview of what is to come or a one-off issue. How much “drama” do you think we get out of the Browns QB competition? Join the conversation! title: Boxer Jake Paul wants to play in the NFL and for the Browns
summary: As a child, you play various sports, and invariably, you pretend to be your favorite player, kicking the winning field goal, making the last-second touchdown grab, hitting the home run with a 3-2 count in the bottom of the ninth, or squeezing the puck on a nutmeg against the goalkeeper. Then you get to high […]
full_text: Jake Paul is on the field at halftime in the game between the New Orleans Saints and the Cleveland Browns at FirstEnergy Stadium on December 24, 2022 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images As a child, you play various sports, and invariably, you pretend to be your favorite player, kicking the winning field goal, making the last-second touchdown grab, hitting the home run with a 3-2 count in the bottom of the ninth, or squeezing the puck on a nutmeg against the goalkeeper. Then you get to high school and realize that every kid on the team is very talented. Instead of hitting dingers to end the game, you are trying to get by the ball to gain first base. RELATED: BROWNS HAVE THE 4 MOST IMPORTANT TYPES OF RECEIVERS Boxer Jake Paul has recently come out and made noise about playing pro football. To be more specific, playing professional football for the Cleveland Browns. This doesn’t seem to be Paul’s attempt at his 15-minutes of fame. Being well-known and well-paid is his current job. And he is pretty good at it. Paul has an estimated net worth between $80 million and $200 million, depending on who’s counting . Paul has stated that several NFL teams are interested in him as a receiver, which is fitting since he played that position and linebacker while at Westlake High School in Westlake, Ohio, just west of Cleveland. He grew up a Browns fan and would like to play for his childhood team. This same scenario happened to former Browns QB Bernie Kosar and WR Paul Warfield. The Browns were their fav team, and they hoped to be drafted by them. And were. It seems that Paul has made it known that he has better hands than most NFL receivers and would make the roster without an issue. For now, teams are already in training camp, so his timing for a workout seems a bit on the later side. Jake Paul tells FOS that he has talked to "a couple [NFL] teams and coaches" who are interested in bringing him on to their roster. "There is a lot of super mediocrity in the NFL. A lot of not-good athletes." pic.twitter.com/eTJQhybAP6 — Front Office Sports (@FOS) July 22, 2026 And don’t say that he wouldn’t be able to take the violence of the NFL game. He had his first boxing match back in 2018. He has headlined a bout against MMA champion Ben Askren and won via a knockout. In his 14 fights, he is 12-2 with seven knockouts. He also defeated Nate Diaz, Anderson Silva, and Tyron Woodley. In 2021, Sports Illustrated named him “Breakout Boxer of the Year.” Paul has been very successful in the business world as well as in music. Currently, Cleveland has 12 receivers on their training camp roster. They selected KC Concepcion in Round 1 and Denzel Boston in the second round of April’s NFL draft. They also signed Tylan Wallace away from the Baltimore Ravens in free agency. It’s easy making the last-second touchdown catch in your backyard with a bunch of neighborhood kids. Paul hasn’t played football since high school. And his boxing career, while with a very good win-loss record, is against retired fighters. NFL players compete each week as their livelihood on the football field. They have their careers invested in this league and aren’t looking for a single payday like a boxer would get paid. This is their career, and many will become well-known for being a pro football player while others become high school coaches or real estate agents. A team like Cleveland is always looking for talent. He could get that call. But it will be as a workout player. If he passes that stage, it becomes a physical and then a training camp contract. With the hope that the real football players won’t find a way to humble a Browns fan turned into a roster hopeful. ( Editor’s Note : All of this feels like a PR stunt and is highly disrespectful to the amount of effort, time, and attention it takes to be a professional athlete of a particular sport. There are very few athletes who are good enough to be professionals at more than one thing (Bo Jackson, Deion Sanders, to name a couple). The Paul family has become elite marketers; this feels like just another example of that.)

title: Cowboys news: Secondary has most to prove at training camp
summary: Cowboys 2026 training camp starts this week, those with the most to prove – Shane Taylor, Inside The Star Will this be the training camp the Cowboys learn what they have in Shavon Revel Jr.? Shavon Revel Jr. Look man, this cornerback room is the worst thing about this team, and they did a great […]
full_text: Nov 3, 2025; Arlington, Texas, USA; Dallas Cowboys cornerback Shavon Revel Jr. (27) celebrates during the game between the Dallas Cowboys and the Arizona Cardinals at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images | Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Cowboys 2026 training camp starts this week, those with the most to prove – Shane Taylor, Inside The Star Will this be the training camp the Cowboys learn what they have in Shavon Revel Jr.? Shavon Revel Jr. Look man, this cornerback room is the worst thing about this team, and they did a great job of getting better this offseason, but this unit has to figure it out. Shavon Revel should feel a lot of pressure, he could either hit a home run or find a backseat over the few weeks starting today. Had it not been for a knee injury that kept him from playing in 2024, Revel Jr. would likely have been a first-round pick. The Cowboys decided to take a swing at him in the third round of last year’s draft, and they’re now in a position to cash in. This group is dealing with a lot of injuries, but the best thing about the Cowboys new defensive coordinator is that Christian Parker knows how to get corners to play at the highest level, and Revel has a real chance to make a name for himself, not just this year, but going forward and that starts this week. New Coaches Look, I could be here all day talking about different players and so on, but how about the new coaches that this staff has? We need to see them with the media there and get these guys fired up and more so on the defensive side and I can’t wait to see the energy on the defense from what Parker is going to bring to the table. I really do think this culture, with the guys they have there now and Jerry Jones letting football finally be that and stopping all the drama is a good thing. If the defense can be average, no reason why, starting this week, this football team shouldn’t be set up to have a good year. Cowboys’ training camp battle presents a best-case scenario that could transform Christian Parker’s defense before season even starts – Mauricio Rodriguez, A to Z Sports The Cowboys need to find out which cornerbacks can hold up in man coverage, which is not something they played a lot at all in 2025, but another area Revel can stand out. The best-case scenario involves Revel Jr. Here’s where it gets fascinating. Even though Revel Jr. is the riskiest bet, he might also represent the best outcome for this defense. Parker comes from a Philadelphia Eagles defense that played man coverage at the highest rate in the NFL in 2025, according to data from Matchquarters.com . And when the Eagles played man, they were the best at it, posting the top EPA per play in man coverage. With Cooper DeJean and Quinyon Mitchell on the outside, Parker’s unit produced the best passing defense in football over the past two seasons. The problem Parker faces in Dallas is that he may not have the personnel to play man coverage at the same rate. The Cowboys are going to run a match defense, which can lean either zone-heavy or man-heavy depending on talent. If the Cowboys’ outside corners can only play zone, Parker loses a critical tool. That is to say, Revel’s development changes everything. Revel’s college tape shows a player who thrived in man coverage. He told DMN in 2025 he spent 90% of his career at East Carolina playing. If he can prove he’s reliable in zone during training camp, which is what the Cowboys will play the majority of the time (even the league-leading Eagles only played man at a 44% rate), Parker suddenly has options. He can go to man coverage when the situation demands it instead of being locked into zone, which is pretty much what Dallas did last year. No.1) Can the defense make this team a contender? – Staff, DallasCowboys.com Finding out what the bar is for the defense based on how well the offense hits the ground running will be fun to follow in Oxnard. Kurt: A common theme has been that if the defense can just be average, the Cowboys should be contenders. But is average good enough? Among the top 10 teams for fewest points allowed in 2025, eight made the playoffs while five of the 10 that were ranked 11th to 20th (or average) reached the postseason. Only one, Chicago at No. 23, made it despite having a subpar defense. So yes, with a good offense, an average defense should contend for a playoff spot. But in terms of raising the Lombardi Trophy, average generally won’t get it done. Over the last 10 seasons, eight of those champions finished in the top 10 for fewest points allowed, and the other two were in the top half of the league. So Dallas already has to make quite a jump from a year ago just to truly contend for the playoffs. To go from dead last in points allowed to winning the Super Bowl? It’s never been done before, meaning the Cowboys would have to take a historical leap. Mickey: Better put, the defense can’t become the No. 1 reason for the Cowboys not contending, and that means not finishing with a winning record; not contending to win the NFC East; not contending to win at least one, maybe two playoff games; not contending for at least their first NFC title since 1995. Because in 2025 that defense cost the Cowboys dearly, at least a winning record, knowing they finished with a playoff-caliber offensive performance, and that includes Dak’s numbers, numbers from their two Pro Bowl wide receivers CeeDee lamb and George Pickens, and a 1,201-yard rushing performance from Javonte Williams, the most single-season rushing yards by a Cowboys running back since 2019 when Zeke finished with 1,357 yards. Cowboys offseason surprisingly drama free, enter training camp more focused – Brian Martin, Blogging The Boys It’s been all about football in the months leading up to camp for the Cowboys, and that is a very refreshing thing. Unlike in the past though, Jerry Jones and Company made their intentions clear in regards to Pickens’ contract situation. Stephen Jones came right out and said “There won’t be negotiations on a long-term deal.” Despite some skepticism, he was true to his word and instead used the franchise tag to secure Pickens’ services for the 2026 season. Now that the July 15 date has passed for the Cowboys to sign George Pickens to a long-term extension, No. 3 will make $27.3 million playing under the franchise tag this season. This put an end to any kind of headline-grabbing storyline in regards to Pickens’ situation, which was really the only potential drama the Cowboys were facing this offseason. Outside the short-lived George Pickens contract saga the only other potential headline-grabbing situation was the pursuit of All-Pro pass rusher Maxx Crosby. Had that come to fruition Dallas once again would’ve likely been the talk of the town, but as we know now that all came to nothing. After a quiet and drama free offseason, Cowboys start training camp Wednesday in Oxnard, California more focused on improving as a team instead of focusing on any outside noise. They can now zero in on improving the offense, rebuilding the defense in Christian Parker’s image, and hopefully getting over the playoff hump (fingers crossed). We seem to be entering a new territory with the Dallas Cowboys and there’s hope this new approach will pay off. It’s going to be really interesting to watch when training camp gets underway. 3 contingency plans every Cowboys fan must prepare for in 2026 – Reid Hanson, The Cowboys Wire Keeping DaRon Bland healthy is of the upmost importance this summer season. Contingency Plan for DaRon Bland Bland, 27, is a former All-Pro coming off back-to-back injured seasons. title: Cowboys offseason surprisingly drama free, enter training camp more focused
summary: When it comes to the Dallas Cowboys, it seems as if the organization corners the market on drama every offseason. This team is continuously on the lips of the media every year and it’s no wonder with an owner like Jerry Jones, who loves/craves the headline-grabbing free publicity. That’s why it’s so surprising things have […]
full_text: When it comes to the Dallas Cowboys, it seems as if the organization corners the market on drama every offseason. This team is continuously on the lips of the media every year and it’s no wonder with an owner like Jerry Jones, who loves/craves the headline-grabbing free publicity. That’s why it’s so surprising things have been so quiet and drama free this offseason. The Dallas Cowboys report to Oxnard, California this week to kick off training camp with zero headline-grabbing stories. This hasn’t been the case in the past. Usually at this time entering training camp the Cowboys are still facing the never-ending contract negotiations with one player or another. In 2023, All-Pro RG Zack Martin missed a portion of training camp attempted to renegotiate his contract. The following year in 2024 contract negotiation surrounded the futures of both Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb, the latter of which ended up missing the majority of training camp before signing an extension. Then just last year there was on the back-and-forth drama between Jerry Jones and Micah Parsons. Parsons eventually requested a trade, which was granted when the Cowboys traded their All-Pro pass rusher to the Green Bay Packers. Things look to be headed the same direction in 2026 with WR George Pickens after a Pro Bowl season. Unlike in the past though, Jerry Jones and Company made their intentions clear in regards to Pickens’ contract situation. Stephen Jones came right out and said “There won’t be negotiations on a long-term deal.” Despite some skepticism, he was true to his word and instead used the franchise tag to secure Pickens’ services for the 2026 season. Now that the July 15 date has passed for the Cowboys to sign George Pickens to a long-term extension, No. 3 will make $27.3 million playing under the franchise tag this season. This put an end to any kind of headline-grabbing storyline in regards to Pickens’ situation, which was really the only potential drama the Cowboys were facing this offseason. Outside the short-lived George Pickens contract saga the only other potential headline-grabbing situation was the pursuit of All-Pro pass rusher Maxx Crosby. Had that come to fruition Dallas once again would’ve likely been the talk of the town, but as we know now that all came to nothing. After a quiet and drama free offseason, Cowboys start training camp Wednesday in Oxnard, California more focused on improving as a team instead of focusing on any outside noise. They can now zero in on improving the offense, rebuilding the defense in Christian Parker’s image, and hopefully getting over the playoff hump (fingers crossed). We seem to be entering a new territory with the Dallas Cowboys and there’s hope this new approach will pay off. It’s going to be really interesting to watch when training camp gets underway. Dallas may not have made any big offseason moves, but through free agency, trades, and this year’s draft picks they’ve overhauled the defense and hopefully upgrade as the roster as a whole. Only time will tell if things will be different though. Are you buying that things are different in Dallas? Or is this just the calm before some kind of storm?

title: Cowboys 2026 roster rundown: DT Jonathan Bullard
summary: While not a former All-Pro like Quinnen Williams or even a Pro Bowler like Kenny Clark, Jonathan Bullard is still their peer as part of the new veteran core in the Cowboys’ defensive front. He won’t be as prevalent in Dallas’ DT rotation, but Bullard could fill important roles in certain formations and as a […]
full_text: While not a former All-Pro like Quinnen Williams or even a Pro Bowler like Kenny Clark, Jonathan Bullard is still their peer as part of the new veteran core in the Cowboys’ defensive front. He won’t be as prevalent in Dallas’ DT rotation, but Bullard could fill important roles in certain formations and as a mentor to one particular rookie. Background Years in NFL: 10 Acquired by: Free agent (2026) Like new teammates Clark and Dak Prescott, Bullard entered the NFL with the 2016 draft class. He was an early third-round pick by the Chicago Bears, playing as a smallish 3-4 DE. Coincidentally, Bullard’s first three seasons in Chicago were as part of a defense run by Vic Fangio, whose name we’ve heard a lot this offseason as the previous boss and mentor to Dallas’ new DC, Christian Parker. Bullard was kept in a rotational, formation-specific role in Chicago and only started five games in three seasons. After being waived by the Bears at final cuts in 2019, he got claimed by Arizona and spent the next three years bouncing from the Cardinals to the Seahawks to the Falcons in backup roles. In 2022, Bullard found stability as a free agent with the Vikings. Their new DC that year, Ed Donatell, had just finished working as the DC in Denver for Fangio during his brief head-coaching run. Back in a familiar scheme, Bullard had his most productive years and emerged as a full-time starter for the first time in his career. He developed a strong reputation for run defense as an edge-setting DE, though without the pass-rushing presence for high stock at his position. Last year, at 31, Bullard signed with New Orleans and was back to a more rotational role. He did have six starts in 15 games, but was generally off the field on perceived passing downs. Back on the market again this past March, Bullard sat available for about two weeks before signing with the Cowboys. Contract Status Years Left: 1 2026 Cap Hit: $1.94 million It’s a fairly minimal deal for a 10-year veteran, but Bullard did get $1.5 million of it guaranteed. That speaks to some solid job security this summer, and the Cowboys likely already having a clear role in mind for him. 2026 Projections Role: Backup DT Roster Chance: 85% The DT position now revolves around Quinnen Williams, leaving guys like Clark, Bullard, Otito Ogbonnia, and LT Overton to fit in where they’re best suited depending on formations and situations. When the Cowboys want beef up front, Clark and Ogbonnia will be the guys. But when they’re looking for more athleticism up front, while not sacrificing too much power, Bullard will likely be the early go-to as Overton continues to develop and transition into a new role. To that end, Bullard is a fantastic mentor for Dallas’ fourth-round rookie. While Bullard was never an edge rusher like Overton was in college, his best work has been at the 4-and-5-tech spots that both will likely play most in Parker’s scheme. If Overton does build up his size and power, he may even get some work inside the way Bullard has throughout his career. The reason we’re leaving some room for Bullard to not make the roster is because of Overton, who just might take to his new role quickly and earn the coaches’ trust. If so, that could make Bullard expendable. It isn’t likely, hence the high probability that he’s on the 53, but what if Overton has a great camp and then some other defensive lineman like Tommy Dunn, Kevin Gilliam, or Jay Toia shows up? At that point, the $1.5 million in guaranteed money may not be enough for Dallas to risk losing a much younger prospect. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. Welcome back and to Day 48 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit a classic Landry-era rivalry game from the heart of the Cowboys-Washington fight for NFC East control. Dallas came into Week 13 at 8-4, Washington arrived at 9-3, and the stakes were simple, the Cowboys needed this one to stay alive in the division race and protect their playoff path. Sunday, December 9, 1973 — 4:00 p.m. ET Texas Stadium, Irving, Texas Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 27, Washington 7 This was also a revenge spot. Earlier in the season, Washington had beaten Dallas 14-7 at RFK Stadium in a bruising Monday night game that ended with Ken Houston stopping Walt Garrison near the goal line as time expired. That loss left the Cowboys feeling like they were still chasing Washington in the division. Two months later, back in Irving, Dallas finally got its answer. The first half was pure rivalry football, tight, physical, and low-scoring. Dallas led only 3-0 at halftime, but the Cowboys were controlling the tone more than the scoreboard showed. Washington’s offense could not get comfortable, and the Dallas defense kept the game exactly where Tom Landry wanted it. The second half is where the Cowboys took over. Roger Staubach spread the ball around and finished for 223 yards, while Calvin Hill powered the offense on the ground and finished with more than 100 rushing yards and two touchdowns. Dallas turned a narrow halftime lead into a commanding win, outscoring Washington 24-7 after the break. Washington’s only points came on a blocked punt long after Dallas had taken control. That detail says a lot about the way the Cowboys defense handled the day. Washington finished with only 155 total yards, 96 net passing yards, 59 rushing yards, nine first downs, and three turnovers. Dallas, meanwhile, produced 414 total yards, 22 first downs, 193 rushing yards, and 221 net passing yards. This game belongs on the countdown because it was the kind of December rivalry win that defined the Landry era. Dallas did not just beat Washington, it dragged the division race back into its own hands. The victory moved both teams to 9-4, split the season series, and set up a final-week race where Dallas still had to finish the job. One week later, the Cowboys beat St. Louis 30-3, won the NFC East at 10-4, and earned home-field advantage throughout the NFC playoffs. #Cowboys vs #Washington 1973 Week 13 Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 27, Washington 7 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/k6lRumwbES — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) July 26, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game The victory was part of a strong closing stretch for Dallas. After a 4-3 start, the Cowboys won six of their final seven regular-season games, then beat the Los Angeles Rams in the divisional round. summary: Year one was quite disappointing for Jaydon Blue. Heading into year two, the RB2 job is up for the taking and Blue will be in a heavyweight […]
full_text: Dallas Cowboys running back Jaydon Blue (23) celebrates after scoring the first touchdown of the game, Sunday, January 4, 2026, in East Rutherford. | Kevin R. Wexler-NorthJersey.com / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Year one was quite disappointing for Jaydon Blue. After reports surfaced during training camp that Blue has some maturity and professionalism concerns, later comments from head coach Brian Schottenheimer seemed to confirm some of those reports. Heading into year two, the RB2 job is up for the taking and Blue will be in a heavyweight fight for the job with Malik Davis, who impressed in limited work in 2025, and Phil Mafah, who the Cowboys seem to be very high on, also heading into year two. In his rookie campaign, Blue put up 129 rushing yards, one touchdown, and one fumble in five games played. He did most of his damage in Week 18 when he rushed for 64 yards and a touchdown against the New York Giants. Blue saw action in four consecutive weeks in weeks five through eight, but a fumble in Dallas’ 44-24 loss to the Denver Broncos seemingly put him back in the doghouse until Week 18. Blue came out of Texas known for his big-play and pass catching ability. While there were certainly signs of that during training camp, in preseason, and in Week 18, the amount of game breaking plays we saw from Blue in the regular season were few and far between. Schottenheimer has spoken highly of Blue’s growth heading into year two. Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer on Jaydon Blue: “He's going to be a huge part of what we want to do, but he's gotta continue to do his part, which he's doing great right now. Night and day from where he was last year…" pic.twitter.com/r4HCikL5Py — 105.3 The FAN (@1053thefan) June 9, 2026 Training camp will be a massive box for Blue to check. With a need for a true RB2 and the comments earlier in the offseason from Schottenheimer, the job is there for the taking. Blue will need to prove himself this offseason, cleaning up some of the fumbling issues, pass protection, and maturity issues that kept him off the field for most of his rookie season. With earlier reports sounding like Blue has taken a step in the right direction, training camp may be the only thing left in the way for Blue to win the job.

title: Cowboys news: 4 names that could see a larger workload in 2026
summary: 4 young Cowboys ready for expanded roles in 2026- Terence Watson, Cowboys Wire Pay more attention to these names heading into the 2026 season. Phil Mafah When a running back brings the size and power Mafah does to the table, it’s only natural to find ways to get him on the field and let him […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - DECEMBER 25: Brevyn Spann-Ford #89 of the Dallas Cowboys carries the ball before the NFL game against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium on December 25, 2025 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images 4 young Cowboys ready for expanded roles in 2026- Terence Watson, Cowboys Wire Pay more attention to these names heading into the 2026 season. Phil Mafah When a running back brings the size and power Mafah does to the table, it’s only natural to find ways to get him on the field and let him wear down opposing defenses. Fans likely would have seen more from the young back last season if not for the shoulder injury that sidelined him until the season finale, in which he punched in a goal-line touchdown. That’s the type of role Mafah needs to carve out for himself as he battles for more snaps this year. Dallas would love to keep starting running back Javonte Williams fresh and healthy throughout the season, and one way to accomplish that is by handing more of the goal-line work to Mafah. At 6-foot-1 and 232 pounds, he has the frame to punish defenders and move the pile in short-yardage situations. It benefits everyone involved. Williams takes fewer unnecessary hits, while Mafah gives the Cowboys a true battering ram in the red zone, someone capable of turning tough yards into touchdowns. Brevyn Spann-Ford Like Mafah, Spann-Ford enters the season behind an established starter in Jake Ferguson. However he managed to carve out a role for himself last year as Dallas’ primary blocking tight end. This season presents an opportunity to expand that role. With Luke Schoonmaker’s standing on the roster far from secure, Spann-Ford has a chance to climb the depth chart if he proves he can be a more consistent receiving threat. The red-zone portion of training camp could be the perfect place to make that statement. Standing 6-foot-7, Spann-Ford presents matchup problems few defenders are equipped to handle near the goal line. Rather than limiting him to blocking duties in those situations, Dallas should look for ways to take advantage of his size and create mismatches in the passing game. He’s shown reliable hands when given opportunities, and expanding his role as a receiver could help the Cowboys become more efficient inside the 20. Before that happens, though, he’ll need to overtake Schoonmaker and establish himself as the clear TE2. 3 Cowboys on the roster bubble who could steal the show in training camp- Maitland Rutledge, The Landry Hat Roster cuts are on the horizon. 3. Traeshon Holden, WR If Cowboys fans should keep an eye on one unknown receiver during training camp, it’s Traeshon Holden. CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, Ryan Flournoy and KaVontae Turpin make up the top of the depth chart, but the fifth WR spot is up for grabs. That spot could be Holden’s if he has just as good a camp as he had last year. Whenever Holden was on the practice field last summer, he made plays. The biggest was a one-handed catch in the back of the end zone on a Joe Milton throw . He also had long catches in the preseason games against the Rams and Ravens. That prompted Dallas to sign him to the practice squad. While he did not see the field in the regular season, he enters camp as one of the favored young receivers to make the team. Dallas brought in veterans like Marquez Valdes-Scantling, Denzel Mims, and Tyler Johnson, but there is no guarantee they make the team. Time is also running out for Jonathan Mingo. Despite all the competition around him, Holden should have a spot at least on the practice squad again if he catches everything thrown his way like last year. Parker Will Get His Chance to Prove Himself I don’t want this to get twisted into Parker being halfway out the door. He hasn’t earned anything yet. I can be rough on defensive coordinators and I think most fans are with me. One week the new guy is a genius, and the next week, after a running back breaks loose for 140 yards, we all want him escorted out of The Star by security. That’s the life of a coach for the Cowboys. The good is good, but bad is the worst in the league for us fans. We can’t operate like that, but we do. We need to give Parker enough time to build his defense instead of patching together someone else’s defense. If the first year is bumpy, we ride those bumps like driving on Oklahoma roads. I want to see if the defense improves, and whether the young guys are developing. Let’s see if his plan makes sense in December, and if it does, keep building… The Dan Quinn Connection is a Whole Thing This hypothetical only works if Washington falls apart, Quinn gets fired and Parker eventually takes a head coaching job. I know that’s a lot of dominoes to fall. Still, Quinn and Schottenheimer aren’t strangers who shared a hallway once. They coached together with the New York Jets in 2007 and 2008 , then reunited in Dallas in 2022 and 2023. Daily discussion question: What is your bold prediction for training camp?

title: Offensive guard Ben Powers agrees to contract restructure
summary: On the night before the Denver Broncos veterans will report for training camp, one tidbit of new information has surfaced. According to 9News insider Mike Klis, the Broncos and left guard Ben Powers have agreed to a restructured contract. Powers was originally slated to account for nearly $18 million dollars against the salary cap for […]
full_text: Oct 5, 2025; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Denver Broncos guard Ben Powers (74) in the tunnel before game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images | Eric Hartline-Imagn Images On the night before the Denver Broncos veterans will report for training camp, one tidbit of new information has surfaced. According to 9News insider Mike Klis, the Broncos and left guard Ben Powers have agreed to a restructured contract . Powers was originally slated to account for nearly $18 million dollars against the salary cap for the 2026 season. However, with the restructure that number is expected to be much lower. While the official particulars have not been released, Klis mentioned there will be a decrease in base salary coupled with an increase in guaranteed money. The ’26 season is the final year of Powers contract. He originally signed with the franchise during the 2023 free agency period to a four-year deal worth $52 million after spending his first four years with the Baltimore Ravens. Last season, Powers missed a significant portion of the season due to a torn bicep injury suffering in Week 5 versus the Philadelphia Eagles. He made his return in mid-December and battled through the rest of the season with a Lisfranc injury—which Klis shined first light on. In three seasons with the Broncos, Powers has started in 40 games and appeared in 42. In that time, the former Oklahoma Sooners standout has allowed 9 sacks and has been penalized just three times. This training camp, it’s expected that Alex Palczewski could seriously challenge for the starting left guard spot. Palczewski played admirably in place of Powers last season and earned himself a lucrative two-year contract extension earlier this offseason. According to OverTheCap , the Broncos had $29 million in cap space prior to this move. With a large number of quality players scheduled to hit free agency after the ‘26 season and a potential Bo Nix extension on the horizon, it’s expected the Broncos’ brass will rollover a large portion of that toward the 2027 season, where they have just $11 million in space.

The good thing about this poll — and its choices — is that it reflects a solid list of returning starters at just about every position, so the camp “battles” are more about depth and future potential for this team. And the interesting thing about the poll winner is which player is WR4? Or even WR3 and WR5? After Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton, Marvin Mims Jr. is probably the third best, but Troy Franklin could really find his groove again with his college QB, and Pat Bryant seems poised for a big leap in year two. full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 26: J.K. Dobbins #27 of the Denver Broncos stiff arms DaRon Bland #26 of the Dallas Cowboys during the second quarter in the game at Empower Field At Mile High on October 26, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Jamie Schwaberow/Getty Images) | Getty Images J.K. Dobbins is heading into his 7th season in the NFL with a checkered, injury-laden career to date. He spent his first four years in the NFL with the Baltimore Ravens, playing in just 24 games in his time there. Dobbins then headed to the Chargers in 2024 and churned out a 905-yard rushing season in 13 games before getting sidelined with an MCL injury. Dobbins joined the Broncos in 2025 and made it 10 games before being put on injured reserve with a Lisfranc injury. Dobbins signed a two-year $16 million extension this year and enters as the #1 RB on the roster, looking to chase that elusive full season of play. Player Profile J.K. Dobbins | Running Back | Denver Broncos Height: 5′ 10″ Weight: 212 pounds Age: 27 years old Experience: 7th season College: Ohio State 2025 stats: 153 rushes for 772 yards (5.0 ypc), 4 TD, 11 receptions 2026 outlook with the Broncos When healthy, Dobbins is an excellent NFL starting running back. He runs with power, has great vision, and is a capable blocker. The Broncos offense last season started hitting its stride midseason with Dobbins and was the best offense we’ve seen in Denver in a very long time in any consistent manner. The question about his durability is still front and center. He’s on a prove-it deal with the Broncos. The Broncos shrewdly drafted a guy in Jonah Coleman who is more than capable of becoming a starting back just in case Dobbins misses time. We’re all knocking on wood, throwing a pinch of salt over our shoulders, and hoping that Dobbins can stay healthy this season, as having a competent running game will go a long way to getting this team back into the playoffs for the third straight season. Final Word There is no doubt in my mind that Dobbins is at the top of the depth chart for the Broncos’ running back roster. He’s a talented ball carrier who forces defenses to stack boxes to slow him down. He churns out runs and is one of the guys I trust to be able to see blocks open up before they happen and hit the hole in time to crank out positive runs. This is a make-or-break season for him at the end of the day. If he can just put together a healthy season for the first time in his career, it will silence a lot of the naysayers. More importantly, it will incentivize the Broncos to extend him to a longer-term contract.

title: Broncos Training Camp Week
summary: Can you believe it? It’s nearly here. After months of offseason waiting and wondering, training camp for the Denver Broncos officially opens on Tuesday (rookies reported last Wednesday). full_text: Can you believe it? It’s nearly here. After months of offseason waiting and wondering, training camp for the Denver Broncos officially opens on Tuesday (rookies reported last Wednesday). All that hand-wringing and those thoughts of “what if” as you fell asleep are finally going to be replaced with actual reporting on our beloved Denver Broncos. There’s plenty to keep an eye on this year. Offensively, in case you have been living under a rock, it’s all about Bo Nix, Jalen Waddle, and Davis Webb. All reports are that Nix’s ankle is back to normal, if not better than ever. Hopefully, Nix’s people thought ahead and sewed up a sock endorsement for him as every camera in a 90-mile radius is going to be trained on that ankle throughout camp. What about Jalen Waddle? Is he finally that big play receiver that can be so sorely needed? Davis Webb assumed play calling duties from Sean Payton, mostly in an attempt to keep him from exploring head coaching opportunities. How long will Payton be able to keep his hands in his pockets before wrestling the playcard back? Defensively, the biggest question is how the Broncos will go about filling the sizable hole left when John Franklin-Myers left for bucketfulls, $63 million worth, of Tennessee Titans cash. Nik Bonitto looks to build upon an incredible 2025 season and 2026 has all the potential for a Pro Bowl calibur season. Then there’s Jonathon Cooper, who is this year’s offseason doofus for getting arrested twice relating to his inability to balance the millions of dollars the Broncos pay him against his personal relationship with his girlfriend. Are you pumped, Broncos Country? The season is still a way’s away, but it’s closer now than it’s ever been. Will the offense take that next step? Can the defense continue it’s league dominance? No matter from which way you look at it, it appears that this season has all the making of a super-special run. Buckle up Broncos Country and keep your hands inside the vehicle, the ride is about to begin.

title: Discussion: Where will the Detroit Lions’ defense rank in 2026?
summary: On Sunday, we discussed the potential of the 2026 Detroit Lions offense. Almost everyone agrees that it will be a top-10 unit in the NFL this season, and per the poll we ran on this site, 90 percent of our audience believes the Lions will have a top-five offense. I’m guessing Lions fans will be […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 20: Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard of the Detroit Lions while playing the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Ford Field on October 20, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Sunday, we discussed the potential of the 2026 Detroit Lions offense. Almost everyone agrees that it will be a top-10 unit in the NFL this season, and per the poll we ran on this site, 90 percent of our audience believes the Lions will have a top-five offense . I’m guessing Lions fans will be a little less optimistic about the other side of the ball. The Lions defense has been an issue for most years under Dan Campbell. While they’ve been able to add some blue chip players like Aidan Hutchinson, Jack Campbell, Kerby Joseph, and Brian Branch, the unit hasn’t been able to put together a full season of strong play. Sometimes, it’s been injuries. Other times, it feels like Detroit is being overcoached. Certainly the lack of a pass rush has been culpable at times. Regardless of the reasoning, the defense has regularly let the Lions down. But could 2026 bring some extra hope? Detroit finally invested in their defensive line, and the players along that front are entering training camp healthier than ever. Additionally, Detroit has fortified their depth at linebacker and safety. And young players like Tyleik Williams, Jack Campbell, and Ennis Rakestraw could elevate their games and jump in their development. That said, there are huge questions about health and starters in the secondary, and Detroit still needs to show they can account and adjust to the losses of DJ Reader, Roy Lopez, Al-Quadin Muhammad, Alex Anzalone, and Amik Robertson. And defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard has a lot to prove in his second season at that position. So today’s Question of the Day is: Where will the Lions’ defense rank in 2026? My answer: First, let’s go back and look at last year’s rankings by several metrics: 5.4 yards per play — 18th 24.3 points per game — 22nd 7.3 yards per pass attempt — 24th 92.5 passer rating — 19th 4.4 yards per carry — 24th 9th in DVOA 15th in EPA per play 11th in success rate In general, this was an average-to-below-average defense. They graded out a little better in advanced statistics—likely because Detroit allowed a high amount of explosive plays that skewed some of the other basic statistics. But despite their surprisingly high DVOA ranking, no one would mistake the 2025 Lions as a top-10 defense. That said, I do think it’s fair to call them average. At times, they were a very good defense, particularly on early downs. What killed them were those explosive plays. They allowed a total of 68 plays of 20+ yards, which was sixth-most in the NFL. Bump that up to 30+ yard plays and Detroit jumps to FIRST, with a league-leading 34 explosives allowed. Point being, if Detroit can manage the frequency of those back-breaking plays, they become a much better defense instantly. Like cutting pop out of your diet, it’s a quick way to trim fat. But that’s a lot easier said than done, and a very easy argument could be made that Detroit’s defensive roster is worse than it was last year. I’m hopeful that Detroit can find a steady—but unspectacular—pairing at safety while Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch recover from injury. I like the overall outlook of the defensive front. I believe Jack Campbell will continue to grow and get better. But I don’t have confidence in anyone else in the linebacker room. The depth at cornerback is perilously thin. And Sheppard still has to prove he can provide logical, effective game plans each week. All of that is to say that I’m not sure expectations should be much higher or lower than last year. If things break the right way (e.g., youth development, injury luck), Detroit’s defense could certainly crack the top-10. For the first two months of last year, Detroit’s defense was playing at a top-10 level. But once the depth got tested, the Lions played some better offenses, and some of Sheppard’s techniques got figured out, the Lions slid quickly. So I’m going to put the Lions right around average in their defense this year with the potential to slide into either the top-10 or bottom-10, but not much beyond that. What are your thoughts? Vote in the poll below and share you full analysis in the comment section below. In order to either, you have to become a member here at Pride of Detroit. It’s easy and it’s free! title: Lions DT Tyleik Williams says he lost an ABSURD amount of weight in 5 months
summary: As Detroit Lions players start to descend upon Allen Park for training camp, one player appears to have gone through a complete body transformation this offseason. Lions defensive tackle Tyleik Williams posted to Instagram on Monday with a caption claiming he has long 50 pounds over the last five months: At the end of the […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - SEPTEMBER 28: Tyleik Williams #91 of the Detroit Lions takes the field during player introductions prior to the game against the Cleveland Browns at Ford Field on September 28, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images As Detroit Lions players start to descend upon Allen Park for training camp, one player appears to have gone through a complete body transformation this offseason. Lions defensive tackle Tyleik Williams posted to Instagram on Monday with a caption claiming he has long 50 pounds over the last five months: On his Instagram page, Lions DT Tyleik Williams claims to have lost 50 pounds in the last five months. pic.twitter.com/eq9gXNN5jh — Jeremy Reisman (@DetroitOnLion) July 27, 2026 At the end of the season, Williams was listed at 328 pounds. Right now, he’s listed at 325 pounds. At this point, it’s unclear if Williams will suddenly drop to under 300 pounds or if he’s talking specifically about body fat that may have been replaced by muscle. UPDATE: Williams provided a little clarity about his weight here, suggesting he weighed more than the Lions’ website had him listed at the end of the year. I was not 328 5 months ago😂😂😂😂😂 let’s relax — Tyleik Williams € (@tyleikk) July 27, 2026 It’s worth noting that his position-mate Alim McNeill went through a similar body transformation early in his career. Back in 2023, McNeill said thanks to a stricter diet and more diligent stretching, he cut his body fat all the way down to 13%. But he stayed around the same 325 pounds that he played in the previous season. What followed was McNeill’s best season to date, posting 32 tackles, 5.0 sacks, 10 quarterback hits, and a career-high 86.8 PFF grade to go with 43 pressures. Last year, the Lions took Williams in the first round of the 2025 draft, and spoke about how they view him very similarly to how they saw McNeill—a college nose tackle that has some untapped potential as a three-tech and pass rusher. “He has a lot of similar traits to Alim McNeill, almost a similar body type,” Lions general manager Brad Holmes said on draft night. “I just think that he–Alim came out more nose tackle-ish, a little bit. Obviously, (he) slimmed his body down (and) became a three-technique. I think [Williams] is kind of coming in closer to that right now.” Are the Lions planning to make a full three-tech transition for Williams? Will he actually come in under 300 pounds or will he just be a “fitter” 325? We’ll have to find out when Lions veterans report for training camp on Tuesday with their first practice scheduled for Wednesday.

title: Kerby Joseph provides some injury insight in series of tweets
summary: On Sunday, the Detroit Lions dropped the disappointing news that Kerby Joseph—along with Brian Branch and tight end Tyler Conklin—would start training camp on the Physically Unable to Perform list. While all three players are eligible to come off the PUP list at any time, it’s still a disheartening development for Joseph, who has been […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 22: Kerby Joseph #31 of the Detroit Lions reacts during an NFL football game against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on September 22, 2025 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Sunday, the Detroit Lions dropped the disappointing news that Kerby Joseph—along with Brian Branch and tight end Tyler Conklin—would start training camp on the Physically Unable to Perform list. While all three players are eligible to come off the PUP list at any time, it’s still a disheartening development for Joseph, who has been dealing with an unspecified chronic knee injury for almost a full year now. On Saturday, Joseph appeared to give a positive update, asking his followers on Twitter “How much yall wanna bet im not on [PUP].” Less than 24 hours later, he was officially put on PUP. Joseph playfully reacted to the news Sunday night, joking on social media that “Yall should’ve bet me.” But after facing considerable backlash on Twitter, he responded to a ton of fans—posting over 50 tweets from 5 p.m. to 11 p.m. ET. While most of them were just clapping back at people who were being confrontational with him, Joseph also had a few tweets in there that offered some insight into what he’s going through. “like right my knee not too good,” Joseph said in one tweet. In his most substantial tweet, Joseph said the following: “I can’t tell yall everything lol… Update fr [for real],” Joseph wrote. “My faith is unbreakable “I can walk now “I’m not in hella pain nomore so I’m not dropping to the floor like the Kansas [City] game “If yall wanna know if I can play this season just ask God … send some prayers also.” That certainly doesn’t sound like a particularly promising development for Joseph, but we’ll hopefully get some clarification when coach Dan Campbell speaks with the media during the team’s first training camp practice on Wednesday. Earlier this offseason, Campbell admitted he didn’t have a clear vision on Joseph’s availability for the 2026 season. “I honestly do not know. I know this, we’ve done everything we can do and he’s done everything he can do to this point,” Campbell said in June. “And we are trying to be as smart as we can and not push this until we absolutely have to because once we’ve done that, then we’ll know one way or another and it’s not worth it right now. “We’re just slowly building, continuing the strength in there. He’s getting treatment. He’s done some of these different things at different places to try to help. So, I feel good about that. I feel good about that we’ve done everything we can and so has he. And so, we won’t know. I mean honestly, we probably won’t know until we get into the thick of training camp.” We’re still a ways away from the “thick” of training camp, so let’s hope Joseph’s outlook improves by then.

title: 2026 Detroit Lions 53-man roster prediction: Erik’s pre-training camp edition
summary: Over the past few weeks, I’ve been rolling out my annual Detroit Lions training camp preview articles, highlighting the camp battles and questions surrounding each position group. With the series coming to its conclusion, and training camp just days away from starting, now is the ideal time for me to share my perspective on the […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - DECEMBER 14: Jared Goff #16 of the Detroit Lions calls a play in a huddle during a 41-34 loss to the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on December 14, 2025 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images Over the past few weeks, I’ve been rolling out my annual Detroit Lions training camp preview articles, highlighting the camp battles and questions surrounding each position group. With the series coming to its conclusion, and training camp just days away from starting, now is the ideal time for me to share my perspective on the team’s 90-man roster. While there is still a ton to be settled with this roster over the next month, this 53-man roster projection is how I believe the Lions would enter the regular season if it started tomorrow. As training camp and the preseason progress, I’ll be updating my projection as the Lions get closer to NFL cutdowns on August 30. But for now, here’s how I see the roster ahead of training camp. Quarterbacks (2) QB Jared Goff QB Teddy Bridgewater QB Luke Altmyer Training camp preview: Can Luke Altmyer force a QB3 role? Altmyer has a steep hill to climb in order to crack the 53-man roster; he’ll either need to jump Bridgewater on the depth chart or convince coaches to keep a QB3 on a loaded roster where spots are at a premium. For now, I’m staying chalk and sticking with the two expected quarterbacks. Running backs (4) RB Jahmyr Gibbs RB Isiah Pacheco RB Sione Vaki RB Jacob Saylors RB Kye Robichaux RB Jabari Small Training camp preview: How RB roles could shift in 2026 Gibbs is expected to expand his RB1 role this season, which opens the door for Pacheco to take on some special teams duties and could result in fewer running backs needed. However, running backs fit a unique role that special teams coordinator Dave Fipp prefers; therefore, I am expecting the Lions to stick with four backs. Wide receivers (5) WR Amon-Ra St. Brown WR Jameson Williams WR Isaac TeSlaa WR Greg Dortch WR Dominic Lovett WR Cedrick Wilson Jr. WR Jackson Meeks WR Tom Kennedy WR Tay Martin WR Lawrence Keys WR Lucky Jackson WR Tarik Black WR Malik Cunningham IR (season-ending): Kendrick Law Training camp preview: WR depth roles up for grabs On the surface, sticking with only five receivers goes a bit against the norm, but when you explore their usage—especially on game days—it lines up more than you might think. After the first four in this section, I have a lot of questions, but I’m not sure the Lions are ready to give up on Lovett just yet, so I went with him as WR5. Can Wilson, Meeks, or Kennedy convince me to keep a sixth? I’m open to the possibility. Tight ends (3) TE Sam LaPorta TE Brock Wright TE Tyler Conklin TE Miles Kitselman TE Zach Horton TE Thomas Gordon Training camp preview: How many TEs will make the roster? Despite Conklin starting training camp on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list , I am still expecting him to slide into the Lions’ TE3 role. His absence will open the door for Kitselman, and the more time Conklin is out, the more time the rookie has to impress. These circumstances could result in a switch at TE3 or maybe even the Lions considering keeping a TE4. For now, I’m sticking with the most common expectations. Offensive tackles (3) OT Blake Miller OT Penei Sewell OT Larry Borom OT Giovanni Manu OT Devin Cochran Training camp preview: Can Blake Miller win the starting RT job? During coach Dan Campbell and general manager Brad Holmes’ time in Detroit, the Lions have started the season with only three offensive tackles on their roster, except for 2024, when Manu was a rookie whom they were developing. Now entering year three, Manu’s development is at a crossroads: prove you can earn a spot as a reliable offensive lineman, or we’ll take the risk you pass through waivers and will place you on the practice squad. Interior offensive linemen (6) RG Tate Ratledge LG Christian Mahogany C Cade Mays G Ben Bartch G/T Miles Frazier C/G Juice Scruggs C Seth McLaughlin G/T Colby Sorsdal C/G Michael Niese G Melvin Priestly G/T Mason Miller Training camp preview: How quickly will Cade Mays adapt to scheme? The Lions spent the offseason prioritizing upgrading and deepening the interior offensive line. They’ve developed their youth, spent money at center, traded for depth, and sought out a veteran for competition. At this time, I am not expecting them to back off any of their investments, leading to them keeping six and keeping the competitions going all season. Defensive tackles (6) DT Alim McNeill DT Tyleik Williams DL Levi Onwuzurike DL Tyler Lacy DT Skyler Gill-Howard NT Jay Tufele DT Mekhi Wingo DT Chris Smith DT Myles Adams NT Aidan Keanaaina DL Tyre West Training camp preview: DT has upgraded starters, questionable depth Based on the Lions’ roster moves on the defensive line, I am expecting some tweaks to how the Lions’ defensive front is deployed. As I touched on in my preview article, the Lions have the option to shift away from a dedicated nose tackle to a more flexible interior, while still leaning on unique fronts, like incorporating a “Big” defensive end. After the Lions’ top three interior players, I selected three players that I believe will fill situational roles, including Lacy at big end, Gill-Howard as a pass-rushing interior tackle, and Tufele as a reserve nose tackle. Those final three roles should be up for grabs in camp. Edge defenders (4) EDGE Aidan Hutchinson EDGE DJ Wonnum EDGE Derrick Moore EDGE Payton Turner EDGE Ahmed Hassanein EDGE Anthony Lucas EDGE Eric O’Neill Training camp preview: 4 big questions at the EDGE The Lions were more aggressive than usual in securing pass rushing options opposite Hutchinson, and the first three players are locked into the roster and likely starting rotation. Beyond those three, I think the Lions will still want a bit more juice for depth and situational purposes. Because of that, I gave the nod to Turner for the EDGE4 role, but I am far from convinced that he will keep the job by the end of camp. First, he’ll need to stay healthy, and second, he’ll need to fend off a group of highly motivated young players. Linebackers (6) LB Jack Campbell LB Derrick Barnes LB Malcolm Rodriguez LB Jimmy Rolder LB Trevor Nowaske LB Damone Clark LB Troy Reeder LB Erick Hunter LB Joe Bachie Training camp preview: Adapting the LB room To see what the Lions linebacker room might look like in 2026 without Alex Anzalone, I went back and studied Week 18 against the Bears, when Anzalone was out due to a concussion. What I saw was Campbell performing typical MIKE duties, while also expanding into coverage over the tight end, Barnes working at the SAM, WILL, and MIKE when Campbell was in coverage, Rodriguez taking on a WILL role, and Nowaske finding the field in a specialized role when the Lions wanted two linebackers at the line-of-scrimmage (essentially deploying two SAM roles about 10% of snaps). While I am not expecting a carbon copy for this year’s group, last year’s Week 18 game did open my eyes to the options the Lions have. What I learned from that game, plus how the roster was constructed this offseason, has led me to believe all four returning linebackers could return to their roles, the investment in Rolder means they keep a fifth, and the emphasis on linebackers on special teams opens the door for Clark to grab a sixth role. Cornerbacks (6) CB D.J. Reed CB Rock Ya-Sin CB Roger McCreary CB Ennis Rakestraw CB Keith Abney CB Khalil Dorsey CB Nick Whiteside CB De’Shawn Rucker DB Aamaris Brown Training camp preview: Nickel sets mean more opportunities for CBs Heading into camp, I have Reed, Ya-Sin, and McCreary in starting roles, Rakestraw as the biggest challenger for a starting job, Abney a potential surprise riser, and Dorsey a key special teams ace. I would have loved to keep a seventh—either saving a spot for a signed veteran not currently on the roster, or an upside youth player—but it’s hard to justify with the other needs on the…

title: Detroit Lions add highly experienced linebacker before training camp
summary: The Detroit Lions had a roster vacancy following the waiving of Teriron Arnold, but instead of filling it with another cornerback, Detroit has opted to add a veteran linebacker. According to sports agency EnterSports Management, the Lions have agreed to terms with Troy Reeder ahead of the start of training camp. Reeder got his start […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - JANUARY 18: Troy Reeder #51 of the Los Angeles Rams stands on the field after an NFL divisional playoff game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on January 18, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions had a roster vacancy following the waiving of Teriron Arnold, but instead of filling it with another cornerback, Detroit has opted to add a veteran linebacker. According to sports agency EnterSports Management, the Lions have agreed to terms with Troy Reeder ahead of the start of training camp. Reeder got his start in the NFL in 2019, signing with the Los Angeles Rams as an undrafted free agent. At the time, Lions general manager Brad Holmes was the Rams’ director of college scouting, so he likely has a good grasp on the type of player and person Reeder is. Since then, Reeder has made an NFL career out of a high amount of special teams play. Reeder would end up making the Rams’ roster in his rookie season and play in all 16 games—including eight starts. Over the following two seasons, he continued to appear in every single game and log an additional 17 starts. He was also part of the Super Bowl-winning 2021 Rams team. After that, he’s jumped from the Chargers to the Vikings, and then landed back with the Rams for the past three seasons. Last year, he appeared in every game for the Rams again, but was almost exclusively on special teams (328 special teams snaps, 81 defensive snaps). In total, Reeder has logged 1,750 special teams snaps and 2,109 defensive snaps over 38 career starts and 106 game appearances. At 6-foot-3, 234 pounds, he’s a bit undersized for a traditional linebacker, but his very strong athletic profile makes him a great special teamer and capable coverage defender. In Detroit, Reeder has a very real chance to make the roster. While the Lions’ top four linebackers are likely set with Jack Campbell, Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez, and rookie Jimmy Rolder, Reeder will compete with the likes Trevor Nowaske and Damone Clark for a reserve/special teams role with the team. UPDATE: Here’s a great article with quotes from Rams defensive coordinator Chris Shula explaining how valuable Reeder was to them last year .
