title: Patriots training camp recap: Intensity dialed down on Day 3
summary: The New England Patriots held their third practice of training camp on Monday on the practice fields behind Gillette Stadium. Tempo slowed down for a shortened walkthrough session as they continue through the five-day ramp up period. Here’s what went down throughout the day. Attendance Returnees: FB Reggie Gilliam (rest) PUP/NFI: ED Gabe Jacas, RB […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - JULY 26: New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel speaks with the team during New England Patriots Training Camp on July 26, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Fred Kfoury III/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New England Patriots held their third practice of training camp on Monday on the practice fields behind Gillette Stadium. Tempo slowed down for a shortened walkthrough session as they continue through the five-day ramp up period. Here’s what went down throughout the day. Attendance Returnees: FB Reggie Gilliam (rest) PUP/NFI: ED Gabe Jacas, RB Terrell Jennings, TE C.J. Dippre, ED Harold Landry III, S Brenden Schooler Injuries: N/A The Patriots active roster featured perfect attendance on Monday as Reggie Gilliam returned after a veteran rest day on Sunday. Five players remained on injured lists, including Gabe Jacas who continues to work through his rehab. “We were going to evaluate him, we are going to see where he is at. This is all part of the process,” Mike Vrabel said before practice. “So, I am again, cautiously optimistic that he will work his way through the return to play, and we will get him back out there.” Takeaways Walkthrough style: As the Patriots often did last season, the intensity was dialed back as players wore bucket hats and sneakers for a jogthrough style of practice after three days of speed work (run tests plus two practices). “This is something that we feel like can help us be able to learn and still develop and install it at different paces,” Vrabel explained. “It was good for us last year. If we can handle that, then hopefully we can continue with this. When we work, we work. I think you guys noticed that. Then being able to come out there today and still act like a professional football team and take care of the details and some of the technique, but just at a different pace.” Players after practice noted the pace helps with the mental side of the game, which then helps them play with more confidence as the work translates back to full-speed. Wide receiver splits: As the offense and defense each split into units across two fields, Drake Maye worked with A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs, Mack Hollins, Kayshon Boutte, and DeMario Douglas consistently throughout the day. In the first session, Kyle Williams was part of that group while Efton Chism III worked on the opposite field. Following a special teams period, the second-year receivers swapped fields for the second full-team session. Maye’s group: With jobs to be won at the third running back and tight end spot, it was notable to see Lan Larison and Tanner Arkin also on the field with Drake Maye. Through three practices, Larison has been the first back to receive carries behind Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson while Arkin has been a consistent presence behind Hunter Henry and Eli Raridon. Offensive lines: It was no surprise to see Will Campbell, Alijah Vera-Tucker, Jared Wilson, Mike Onwenu, and Morgan Moses protecting Drake Maye from left-to-right. In front of DeVito, Andrew Rupcich served as the center with Ben Brown and Caedan Wallace at his sides. Tackle duties were then mainly left for Marcus Bryant and Caleb Lomu, who continues to show his versatility. “Try to get him some jumbo tight end work, and he will play some tackle, he will play some guard,“ Vrabel said of Lomu. ”We are just going to look at some versatility and see where he fits and how he can help us, but there will be a lot of things that are going to be new to him and some techniques that are different and run schemes and pass protection.“ Other notes: In a reoccurring theme through three days, the offense continued to practice tempo even in a slower setting. QB coach Ashton Grant served as the offensive coordinator on the second field. Tempo will increase as the Patriots retake the practice fields on Tuesday for Day 4 of camp which is set to start at 10:15 a.m. ET.

title: Patriots training camp primer: Day 3 practice preview, schedule, more
summary: For a third day in a row, the New England Patriots will hit the practice fields on Monday. That’s right, it’s time for training camp session No. 3 this summer — one that will tone the intensity down a bit compared to the last two days: the expectation is that it will be a walkthrough […]
full_text: Jul 25, 2026; Foxborough, MA, USA; New England Patriots tight end Hunter Henry (85) and tight end Jeremiah Franklin(80) during a drill at training camp at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images | Eric Canha-Imagn Images For a third day in a row, the New England Patriots will hit the practice fields on Monday. That’s right, it’s time for training camp session No. 3 this summer — one that will tone the intensity down a bit compared to the last two days: the expectation is that it will be a walkthrough rather than a fully-competitive session. Nonetheless, there will still be plenty of action in Foxborough. Welcome to Day 3. Schedule As usual, the Patriots’ third training camp practice of the summer will take place on the fields behind Gillette Stadium. The session is free and open for the general public to attend. 9:15 a.m. ET: Gates open 9:30 a.m. ET: Mike Vrabel press conference 10 a.m. ET: Practice (walkthrough) ca. 12 p.m. ET: Player availability (WR A.J. Brown, WR DeMario Douglas, OT Morgan Moses, ED Bradyn Swinson, S Craig Woodson, K Andy Borregales) As always, of course, the schedule is tentative and subject to change. For more information, please visit our Pats Pulpit Training Camp Guide . Story of the day What will the depth chart look like? With a walkthrough scheduled for Monday, the Patriots will tone down the intensity and focus more on position groupings and mental work than physical competition. This, in turn, will give us a chance to see how those groups currently stack up on both sides of the ball. The first two days of practice might have earned some players a higher number of quality reps. Injuries to monitor NFI: RB Terrell Jennings, S Brenden Schooler PUP: TE C.J. Dippre, ED Harold Landry III, ED Gabe Jacas TBD: FB Reggie Gilliam The Patriots’ physically unable to perform list saw an addition on Sunday. Second-round draft pick Gabe Jacas, who had signed his rookie contract earlier that day, was sent there to start his rookie training camp . Like the rest of the other players on that or the non-football injury/illness list, he can be activated and stat practicing at any point without any lead-up. Meanwhile, fullback Reggie Gilliam was nowhere to be seen on Sunday. Players to watch With the Patriots running a walkthrough, we will be looking mostly on depth charts and packages rather than who performs at a certain level. With that said, here are our player to watch. RB Jam Miller: Even though Lan Larison lined up as the third running back up on Sunday, Miller had the more impressive moments as a rotational RB4; he had multiple long runs while working with the second and third units. The competition at the position will become more intense as soon as full pads are introduced to the mix later this week, but the seventh-round rookie appears to keep building a strong foundation beforehand. TE Tanner Arkin: The undrafted free agent might be the frontrunner to earn the No. 3 tight end spot behind Hunter Henry and Eli Raridon. A blocker first, he saw reps with the first-team offense on Sunday and also lined up at fullback in place of the absent Reggie Gilliam. Will Tuesday be a continuation of that usage? ED Xavier Holmes: The undrafted rookie has had a good start to his first NFL training camp, regularly providing pressure on the second and third teams. Can he keep stringing positive moments together, and if so earn himself a promotion to the first-team rotation with Harold Landry and Gabe Jacas both sidelined? Pats Pulpit will have you covered throughout the day, so please make sure to regularly check back to patspulpit.com for all the latest news from camp. title: Will Campbell carrying lessons from NFL vets into Patriots training camp
summary: New England Patriots left tackle and 2025 first-round draft selection Will Campbell took advantage of opportunities outside of the organization this offseason, training with NFL veterans in Dallas, he told media members on Sunday. “A ton of knowledge,” Will Campbell said after Sunday’s practice about what he took away from the experience. “I work with […]
full_text: Jun 10, 2026; Foxborough, MA, USA; New England Patriots offensive tackle Will Campbell (66) does a drill with offensive tackle Lorenz Metz (72) during minicamp at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images | Eric Canha-Imagn Images New England Patriots left tackle and 2025 first-round draft selection Will Campbell took advantage of opportunities outside of the organization this offseason, training with NFL veterans in Dallas, he told media members on Sunday. “A ton of knowledge,” Will Campbell said after Sunday’s practice about what he took away from the experience. “I work with a lot of guys who have been around a long time and done it at a high level for a long time. So just anything that they could teach me that could help me. “Or whether that’s football or off the field, or just training and just being around in the same environment. I always want to put myself in the best position possible.” Lane Johnson, Tristan Wirfs, Rashawn Slater and New York Jets 2025 first-round pick Armand Membou invited Campbell south of Foxboro, where the group trained with the world’s strongest man, Mitchell Hooper, and a former Navy SEAL. While training, Campbell strengthened his relationships with the veterans who were present, saying he feels that he can always reach out to them if needed. Before traveling to Dallas, the 22-year-old told the media during voluntary OTAs that he underwent physical therapy five days a week throughout the offseason to recover from a torn MCL in 2025. Campbell suffered the injury during Week 12 against the Cincinnati Bengals. Still, the second-year lineman quickly returned for New England’s postseason run, but his effectiveness dipped during those final five contests. In his first 12 games last season, Campbell posted a 76.1 pass-blocking grade on Pro Football Focus ; however, that number drastically decreased to 39.2 following the injury. Entering training camp, the LSU product said he’s feeling “great” when asked about his recovery. “It’s exciting,” Campbell said about being back in Foxboro. “[It’s] good to be back. Good to see everybody. [I’m] excited about what we have, and I’m ready to go.” One of Campbell’s goals for the summer sessions is to further build his chemistry with starting left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker, who was signed to a multi-year deal in free agency . Though the two are still early in that process, as Vera-Tucker was limited in his participation through most of the spring, recovering from a torn triceps. “Just continue to grow every day,” Campbell said of his goals. “Just me and [Alijah Vera-Tucker] continuing to get comfortable playing next to each other and just doing my job to the best of my ability.” The left-side tandem will look to build on the Patriots’ offensive line improvement from 2025.

title: Saints announce year-long celebration to honor six decades of football in New Orleans
summary: On Monday, July 27, the New Orleans Saints announced their plans to commemorate the team’s 60th season with a yearlong celebration honoring six decades of football while looking ahead to the future of the Black and Gold. The celebration will feature commemorative branding, exclusive merchandise, fan experiences, digital storytelling, community activations, and special tributes throughout […]
full_text: On Monday, July 27, the New Orleans Saints announced their plans to commemorate the team’s 60th season with a yearlong celebration honoring six decades of football while looking ahead to the future of the Black and Gold. The celebration will feature commemorative branding, exclusive merchandise, fan experiences, digital storytelling, community activations, and special tributes throughout the 2026 season. The 2026 season represents one of the most significant years in franchise history, as the Saints celebrate not only their 60th season, but also the 20th anniversary of the Black and Gold’s return to the Caesars Superdome. The year will also feature the Pro Football Hall of Fame induction and ring ceremony for Drew Brees, Saints Hall of Fame inductions of Mark Ingram II and Terron Armstead, and the franchise’s participation in the NFL’s first-ever regular season game in Paris, accompanied by a New Orleans watch party that will allow local fans to be part of the historic occasion. Saints Owner and CEO Gayle Benson said, “For 60 seasons, the New Orleans Saints have been a source of pride, resilience and unity for both our city and the entire region. The unwavering passion of our fans, the dedication of our players and coaches, and the strength of the New Orleans community have shaped our history every step of the way. This season is a celebration of where we’ve been, who we are and all that lies ahead as we continue building on the proud tradition of Saints football.” The celebration officially begins during 2026 Training Camp, where 60th season branding will appear throughout Saints Training Camp presented by Rouses at the Ochsner Sports Performance Center and Saints Training Camp presented by Entergy at Tulane University. Training Camp attendees will receive a complimentary 60th season commemorative poster upon entry, while season ticket holders had the opportunity to select exclusive 60th season merchandise as part of this year’s membership gift. The team will also showcase 60 seasons of Saints football digitally by highlighting defining moments in franchise history through an interactive timeline, while commemorative street banners featuring the 60th season logo will line Poydras Street in downtown New Orleans. Starting in September, the Saints will continue the celebration with the debut of Saints at 60, a six-part documentary series highlighting the people who have helped shape the franchise over six decades. Each episode will feature the stories of fans, media members, Cheer Krewe, halftime performers and many others whose passion has helped define Saints football. Additional programming during the opening month of the season includes: The 60th season logo illuminated on the gold exterior lighting of Caesars Superdome leading into every home game. Black and Gold Week will lead us into the start of the season and Black and Gold Fridays also kick off the week of September 7. A Saints season-opening watch party at Manning’s presented by Caesars and Sire Spirits on Sunday, September 13. The annual Saints 5K presented by Hancock Whitney and the Kids Fun Run presented by Ochsner Children’s on Saturday, September 26, featuring commemorative 60th season race shirts and finisher medals. A limited-edition 60th season commemorative coin giveaway in partnership with Caesars for the September 27 home opener. The debut of the club’s exclusive 60th season retail capsule collection. The introduction of new hometown culinary favorites inside Caesars Superdome, further enhancing the gameday experience. The return of Team Ambassadors on gamedays, continuing one of the NFL’s nationally recognized fan engagement programs. The 60th season celebration will remain visible the entire season across every aspect of the Saints gameday experience. Players and mascots will wear commemorative 60th season uniform patches, while branding will appear on field markings, stadium signage, digital platforms and on the Saints mobile app. Player introduction videos will also blend current stars with iconic moments and legendary Saints players, celebrating the franchise’s rich history while embracing its future. Fans will also find an expanded collection of commemorative merchandise during the season as the Saints continue strengthening their position as a lifestyle brand. The club will spotlight partner collections and special retail events prior to home games, including collaborations with Bomb Designs and Sneaker Politics. The official 60th season commemorative coin will also remain available throughout the season at Saints retail locations. As part of the Saints training camp experience, season ticket holders will receive exclusive early access to reserve complimentary tickets for the newly added Jaguars and Tulane joint practices beginning Monday, July 27, before tickets become available to the general public on Tuesday, July 28. Admission to both practices will be complimentary while supplies last. For more details, please visit Saints Training Camp 2026 Tickets

title: Kellen Moore is up for a career-defining season in 2026
summary: The focus around the New Orleans Saints for the 2026 season often revolves around the exciting development of second-year quarterback Tyler Shough. Still, there is another second-year Saint that some may be overlooking: Kellen Moore. Moore is entering his second season as a head coach in the NFL and is already being praised despite coaching […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - NOVEMBER 23: Kellen Moore of the New Orleans Saints looks on from the sideline during an NFL football game against the Atlanta Falcons at Caesars Superdome on November 23, 2025 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The focus around the New Orleans Saints for the 2026 season often revolves around the exciting development of second-year quarterback Tyler Shough. Still, there is another second-year Saint that some may be overlooking: Kellen Moore. Moore is entering his second season as a head coach in the NFL and is already being praised despite coaching the black and gold to a 6-11 record in 2025. The team’s strong 5-4 finish is enough to keep the fans excited and the media interested, but 2026 will be a career-defining year for the young head coach. The Super Bowl-winning playcaller has his choice of quarterback as the starter, and the roster is starting to take shape as the vision he sold to the front office when he got the job. From adding an explosive running back in free agency with Travis Etienne to putting a superstar talent at wide receiver with a top-10 pick in the draft next to Chris Olave, Moore is building an offense of his dreams. But with excitement comes pressure. The Saints are now expected to perform the best they have in years, and anything short of it will bring up plenty of questions on Moore’s ability to coach and the Saints’ future altogether. If Shough looks poor, he’ll be a 27-year-old struggling second-year quarterback with not much room to grow. Criticism will be on the team’s “all in” approach on offense, citing the multiple big deals the team made in free agency with the idea that Shough is the guy. And despite being an offensive coach, if the team were to perform poorly on defense, Moore won’t be fully excused for the struggles. Moore took an offensive-heavy approach in his second offseason with the team, adding less talent than what left in free agency. Sure, they added some strong names such as Kaden Ellis, but New Orleans’ main focus was surrounding their young quarterback with talent. While a strong-performing offense would likely keep Moore off the hot seat, his approach to building the roster wouldn’t be free from the rough New Orleans criticism if the defense can’t play at a high-level, a level we saw them play at in 2025. Despite all the pressure, a strong season by Moore and the Saints would be monumental for both sides. The Saints have been a bottom-half team in the NFL since Brees’ departure, and fans are getting restless. Moore and Shough have brought back the spark that had slowly drifted away during that span. Football is everything to New Orleans. The gumbo tastes better, and crime is down when the Saints are good. While they rightfully aren’t projected to be Super Bowl contenders in 2026, Moore has the chance to make the black and gold competitive again and has the opportunity to win the NFC South. Expectations are high for Moore, and he’s up for the challenge.
author: Kyle Besson

title: Kaden Elliss could be the key to Brandon Staley’s Saints defense
summary: As the New Orleans Saints prepare to open the 2026 season on the road against the Detroit Lions, much of the attention has centered on defensive coordinator Brandon Staley and how he’ll fill the void of Demario Davis. According to New Orleans Football Network’s Nick Underhill, one player could be more important to that transition […]
full_text: TAMPA, FL - DECEMBER 5: Kaden Elliss #55 of the New Orleans Saints runs downfield during an NFL football game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium on December 5, 2022 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images As the New Orleans Saints prepare to open the 2026 season on the road against the Detroit Lions, much of the attention has centered on defensive coordinator Brandon Staley and how he’ll fill the void of Demario Davis. According to New Orleans Football Network’s Nick Underhill, one player could be more important to that transition than anyone else: veteran LB Kaden Elliss. Speaking alongside Mike Triplett, Underhill explained why he believes Elliss is the focal point of what Staley wants to accomplish defensively. “Elliss is interesting because I think that he is the piece Staley’s looking at as the straw that stirs the drink a little bit,” Underhill said. “I think he views him as like, here’s my first handpicked chess piece. Like I can do all this stuff with him.” Underhill believes Elliss’ versatility makes him uniquely valuable in Staley’s defensive scheme, which has historically relied on defenders capable of filling multiple roles. Whether it’s rushing the passer, dropping into coverage or lining up in different spots across the front seven, Elliss gives Staley the flexibility to disguise looks and create favorable matchups. “I think he opens up the defense and gives them versatility that if he disappeared, I don’t know what you would… I don’t know how that would change,” Underhill continued. “That is a big one because it does feel like he is a little bit more so, positional value aside, like a Jenga block on the defense and that, like if he vanishes, where do you go?” The comparison stresses just how critical Elliss is to the Saints’ defensive identity, especially following the departure of Demario Davis this offseason in free agency. Rather than simply replacing his production if an injury were to occur, losing Elliss would force Staley to rethink how he deploys the entire defense. As training camp gets underway, all eyes will be on how Staley utilizes Elliss. If Underhill’s assessment proves accurate, the linebacker won’t just be another starter, but could be the player who makes the Saints’ defensive scheme come to fruition.

title: NY Giants news: Training camp is almost here
summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are your headlines for Monday, as we gear up for the beginning of training camp on Wednesday. full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are your headlines for Monday, as we gear up for the beginning of training camp on Wednesday. Every NFL Roster’s Biggest Strength and Weakness Before 2026 Preseason | Bleacher Report Biggest Strength: Pass Rush. The New York Giants won’t be a fun obstacle for opposing quarterbacks this offseason. They already had three talented edge-rushers in Brian Burns, Abdul Carter, and Kayvon Thibodeaux, and they added Ohio State’s Arvell Reese to the group in April. While the Giants plan to use Reese as an off-ball linebacker as a rookie, he will add a new dynamic to the pass rush. Expect to see new defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson lead with his pass rush this season. Biggest Weakness: Defensive Tackle. While Dennard should benefit from having a terrific pass-rushing rotation, his group may struggle to control the line of scrimmage. New York’s defensive tackle rotation took a massive hit when Schoen traded Dexter Lawrence to the Bengals, and it took another big one when Roy Robertson-Harris suffered a torn ACL during OTAs. New York has added the likes of Shelby Harris, D.J. Reader, and Leki Fotu, but the interior of its defensive front figures to be a 2026 liability. West Virginia is not going to be a vacation trip John Harbaugh practices are not for the faint of heart 😅 @judybattista | @JamieErdahl | @Giants pic.twitter.com/42UeQDkyJY — Good Morning Football (@gmfb) July 27, 2026 These are Giants’ biggest questions entering John Harbaugh’s first training camp | NJ.com How will Giants handle the camp grind? Harbaugh is going to run a much tougher camp than Brian Daboll. That much we knew from the moment the Giants hired Harbaugh. How much of a grind will it be? Well, the Giants practice four straight days to open camp. Then they have an off day. Then they practice six straight days before their next off day. Will this help push the Giants into elite game shape? Or cause injuries? Ranking the Giants’ 6 most indispensable players: Who can they least afford to lose? | The Athletic Defense. 1. OLB Brian Burns. Not only is Burns a top-tier pass rusher who tallied an NFC-best 16.5 sacks last season, but he’s also a highly respected veteran within the Giants locker room. Just look at the turnout of teammates who showed up for his charity softball game this spring. So yes, he might be part of one of the best position rooms on the team, which hurts his case for being the most indispensable, but his presence as the face of the defense — especially with Dexter Lawrence out of town — isn’t as easily replaceable. PFF Tackle Rankings: The top 32 players ahead of the 2026 NFL season | PFF 7. Andrew Thomas, New York Giants. When healthy, Thomas is one of the top blindside protectors in the NFL. The primary issue is that he has eclipsed 900 snaps just once in the past five seasons. However, in his 13 games played in 2025, Thomas tied for fourth place among qualified tackles with a 90.3 PFF grade. He allowed just 13 total pressures, including one sack, while posting a career-high 84.5 PFF run-blocking grade. A consistently healthy Thomas gives the Giants their best chance to compete in a tough NFC East. All-Under-25 Team: Drake Maye, Abdul Carter among NFL’s ascending young players entering 2026 season | NFL.com Edge, Abdul Carter, Age 22. Carter arrived with great expectations as a top-three pick and attracted attention for his winding journey toward selecting a jersey number, then seemed to fly under the national radar throughout most of his rookie season. Those paying closer attention, however, understood that Carter had a strong debut campaign. Despite recording just four sacks in 2025, Carter finished seventh in quarterback pressures with 72 (per NGS), just five fewer than Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett recorded. He earned enough Defensive Rookie of the Year votes to finish fifth, and if he can convert more of his pressures into sacks, he’ll quickly climb the popularity charts. He turns 23 in October, too, so he has plenty of time to do so. Sisi Mauigoa on getting ready for his first camp . @NikiLattarulo talks with Giants first-rounder Francis Mauigoa at Citi Field about his first training camp and working with Jaxson Dart ➡️ @Honda pic.twitter.com/qf6rCTTDZM — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) July 26, 2026 NFL training camp storylines: Aaron Donald watch, QB battles, rookie breakouts among NFC questions | CBSSports.com How good does Malik Nabers look coming off a torn ACL? The New York Giants need Pro Bowl wide receiver Malik Nabers healthy in order to maximize 2025 first-round pick quarterback Jaxson Dart’s development. Nabers is far and away the most important developing story at Giants training camp. Nabers’ torn ACL injury wasn’t cut and dry. It also included a full meniscus repair and an extra procedure to remove inflamed scar tissue. However, New York did not place Nabers on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list to begin training camp, which provided some hope that he might be ready to roll for Week 1. When he’s on the field, he’s dangerous: Nabers’ 127 career receptions through 19 career games rank as the second-most in NFL history behind only his Giants teammate Odell Beckham Jr.’s 133. New York needs Nabers to be back at full strength, and how he looks in training camp will be far and away the most important development for the Giants. title: Massive renovation, expansion of NY Giants’ headquarters underway
summary: The New York Giants on Monday announced the extent of a massive renovation project at their East Rutherford, N.J. headquarters. In a statement released by the team, the Giants say the renovations will “expand and transform their team headquarters, anchored by a new and modern football-focused facility designed to elevate player performance, preparation, and recovery.” […]
full_text: The New York Giants on Monday announced the extent of a massive renovation project at their East Rutherford, N.J. headquarters. In a statement released by the team, the Giants say the renovations will “expand and transform their team headquarters, anchored by a new and modern football-focused facility designed to elevate player performance, preparation, and recovery.” Work began several months ago, and is expected to be completed in advance of the 2028 season. “This is a significant investment in the future of our football operation,” said Giants President and CEO John Mara in a statement released by the team. “We believe it is our responsibility to provide our players, coaches, and staff with the resources and environment they need to succeed. As the game continues to evolve, we must continue to evolve with it. This project reflects our commitment to our people and to building a foundation that will support the New York Giants for years to come.” The project will include approximately 93,500 square feet of new construction and 46,000 square feet of renovations. Enhancements include: Expanded locker room spanning more than 6,000 square feet, featuring 100 full-size lockers State-of-the-art weight room with more than 11,000 square feet, including a nutrition bar and cardio mezzanine overlooking the indoor field Advanced sports medicine and rehabilitation space tripling the current footprint Integrated recovery and wellness areas, including hydrotherapy, steam, sauna, red light therapy, cryotherapy, dry float tanks, and hyperbaric chambers. Modernized player and team areas supporting preparation throughout the week “From the outset, our goal was to create a space that reflects who we are as an organization while pushing forward into what’s next”, said Jonathan Tisch, Treasurer of the New York Giants. “Every design decision was made with purpose — from how players move through the building to how a team connects and collaborates. This is about creating an environment that feels distinctly Giants and gives our players and staff everything they need to succeed.” The Giants recently completed renovating and expanding their cafeteria. The ongoing construction is a major part of the reason why the Giants moved this year’s training camp, which begins on Wednesday, to The Greenbrier Resort in West Virginia. Construction around the Meadowlands Complex for the recently-concluded World Cup was also a factor in the decision to move training camp. The decision to move camp to West Virginia was made before the Giants hired John Harbaugh as head coach.

full_text: Defensive tackle Marlon Davidson during a preseason game | Getty Images The New York Giants are signing veteran defensive tackle Marlon Davidson , per a report from Jordan Raanan of ESPN , and tight end Tyler Moore , per Mike Garafolo . Davidson, 28, was a second-round pick by the Atlanta Falcons in the 202 NFL Draft. He only played two seasons for the Falcons, playing in 19 games in 2020 and 2021 with one start. He played in five games with three starts in 2023 for the Tennessee Titans, and played in one game last year for the Houston Texans. His career has largely been derailed by injuries. His 2022 season was ended by knee surgery, while his 2024 season was ended by a biceps injury. Davidson was considered a plus pass rusher as a prospect with scheme and alignment diversity coming out of Auburn. He weighs in at roughlty 6-foot-3, 300 pounds and will likely be a 5-technique defensive end in a three-down front of a B-gap defender for the Giants. He fills one of the roster spots opened when the Giants waived linebacker Cam Jones and defensive tackle C.J. Ravenell. Moore is an undrafted free agent out of Indiana. Per the league’s official transaction report, the Giants worked out 18 players before departing for The Greenbrier Resort in West Virginia, where training camp will begin on Wednesday. title: Vita Vea trade request: Should the Giants be interested?
summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers got some unwelcome news on Monday as veteran defensive tackle Vita Vea reportedly requested a trade, per Adam Schefter. The trade request, which was first reported by Adam Schefter, comes as Vea is entering the final year of a 4-year, $71 million contract. The New York Giants, meanwhile, are still looking […]
full_text: Tampa Bay Buccaneers nose tackle Vita Vea makes a tackle | Getty Images The Tampa Bay Buccaneers got some unwelcome news on Monday as veteran defensive tackle Vita Vea reportedly requested a trade, per Adam Schefter . The trade request, which was first reported by Adam Schefter, comes as Vea is entering the final year of a 4-year, $71 million contract. The New York Giants, meanwhile, are still looking for solutions to fill the void in their defensive line left by the trade of star nose tackle Dexter Lawrence. Vea’s request is likely a part of his contract negotiations. However, as the Giants well know, these things have a way of quickly going from leverage play to reality. That of course, begs the question: Should the Giants be in on a potential trade of Vea? Vea, 31, remains one of the best interior defensive linemen in the NFL. Even across the 30-year mark, he combines rare size, burst, and power for a nose tackle. The Giants did sign DJ Reader earlier this off-season and also drafted Bobby Jamison-Travis. However, neither is of the same caliber as the former 12th overall pick. Adding Vea would The question, of course, comes down to price. Vea is 31, a nose tackle, and seeking a contract extension. The Giants likely won’t want to trade a high draft pick, considering the expected caliber of the 2027 NFL Draft. For reference, even the New England Patriots only parted with a 2028 pick for AJ Brown. Vea simply doesn’t have the kind of impact potential that Brown does, so the Buccaneers would likely have to settle for less than they’d prefer. It’s possible that the Giants could negotiate a favorable deal given Vea’s age. Perhaps they could negotiate a price that uses picks later round picks over the 2027 and 2028 drafts. Or perhaps they could also perhaps use Kayvon Thibodeaux as a trade chip. In that case, they may ask for additional compensation considering the fact that Thibodeaux is only 25 and plays a more valuable position. Regardless, the feeling here is that Joe Schoen absolutely should pick up the phone. So Giants fans, do you think the Giants should seriously consider a trade for Vea?

title: Revisiting the NY Giants 2024 draft class
summary: It isn’t often that an entire draft class emerges as contributors. It happened for the New York Giants back in 2007, with each of their picks playing meaningful roles in their Super Bowl run. It might have happened again with the Giants’ 2024 draft class. While the team wanted to move up and dip into […]
full_text: ﻿New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers catches a touchdown pass against the Philadelphia Eagles. | Eric Hartline-Imagn Images It isn’t often that an entire draft class emerges as contributors. It happened for the New York Giants back in 2007, with each of their picks playing meaningful roles in their Super Bowl run. It might have happened again with the Giants’ 2024 draft class. While the team wanted to move up and dip into a historic quarterback draft class, they won just enough to be drafting fifth overall and out reach of the top quarterback prospects. Instead, they reinforced the rest of their roster around the quarterback position. The 2024 class paid immediate dividends and while the season fell apart for the Giants, the class itself was lauded as one of the very best in the NFL after the season ended. Unfortunately, the collapse continued into 2025 and much of that class took a step back. As we did with the 2023 draft class, we’re going to go back and see what we were saying about the 2024 draft class immediately after the season, catch up to where they are now, and look at how John Harbaugh’s new staff can help them take a step forward in 2026. ( The quoted text is drawn from our rookie report card from the end of the 2024 season, linked below ) WR Malik Nabers The Giants selected the star receiver over quarterbacks J.J. McCarthy, Michael Penix Jr., and Bo Nix. The jury is out on McCarthy due to his knee injury, but Nix lightly pushed Jayden Daniels for Offensive Rookie of the Year in the middle parts of the season, and Penix Jr. flashed in his second start last week. Should the Giants have gone with their favorite of the three to fix this Giants’ quarterback room? It’s certainly difficult to definitively say no, but Nabers as a “ consolation ” prize is a best case scenario. Nabers broke Odell Beckham Jr.’s franchise rookie reception record and now has 104 catches with one game to go on the season. He has caught 104 on 162 targets for 1,140 yards with six touchdowns. Nabers is 165 yards away from tying Beckham’s rookie season yardage mark. He could plausibly do that in Week 18 against Philadelphia, although that would be his second highest single-game mark on the season. The Giants found a true wide receiver one in Malik Nabers. He can effectively play X, Z, or in the slot. He can win any matchup and he finds ways to secure contested catches thrown in his area code. He’s a difference maker, and an explosive threat the Giants lacked for years. If the Giants can locate a competent quarterback, Nabers will solidify himself as a top-five wide receiver in the NFL. Grade: A Mid-season Grade: A The big question going into 2026 with Nabers is his health. Athleticism is the core of his game and while he’ll be avoiding the PUP list, we don’t know how Nabers will be performing to start the season or how soon he’ll be approaching full strength. From a player development standpoint, the big thing Nabers needs to work on is (somewhat surprisingly) his play at the catch point. Depending on the accounting, he’s had between 10 and 12 drops in 17 career games, a drop rate of 7.3%, and a contested catch rate of 45.7%. It’s certainly true that Nabers has had to make due with poor quarterback play in his time as a pro, so he definitely deserves some grace for his drop rate. However, his contested catch rate is also right in line with his play from college — when he had Jayden Daniels as his quarterback and was going against college corners. There isn’t much that wide receivers coach Chad Hall and passing game coordinator Brian Callahan can do until Nabers can get back up to speed. However, doing his work in the classroom can help from the mental side of things. Continuing to improve his coverage recognition, understanding of leverages and defensive techniques, and working with Jaxson Dart to ensure they’re always on the same page will go a long way to making sure he can maximize his catch windows. S Tyler Nubin Nubin quickly seized the starting safety spot over Dane Belton after the rookie missed the first few weeks of training camp. He led the Giants’ defense in snaps and was second behind Bobby Okereke in tackles before he suffered a season-ending ankle injury that required surgery. Nubin was placed on IR three games after the mid-season report card. The rookie remains second in tackles on the Giants with 98; Micah McFadden leads the team with 107 tackles. Nubin has not played since the New Orleans loss but he still leads all rookie defenders in tackles. I am optimistic about Nubin. He flies around the field with controlled aggression and displays elite short-area quickness around the line of scrimmage. However, he only earned one pass defensed through his entire rookie season. — Nubin had 11 passes defended and 13 interceptions in college. Grade: B Mid-season Grade: B Nick wasn’t the only writer to praise Nubin’s speed on the field at the end of his rookie season. And while Nubin didn’t record an interception, he did hold opposing quarterbacks to a 65% completion. That’s a very good mark for a safety, considering Xavier McKinney allowed 73% completion in his 8 INT season. Since then, however, Nubin has been heavily criticized for his speed on the field, his completion percentage allowed has risen to 73%, and he still hasn’t recorded an interception. Additionally, where Nubin was one of the NFL’s best tacklers in his rookie season, his tackling regressed significantly in 2025. Considering his much-criticized athleticism is still on par with several Pro Bowl and All-Pro caliber safeties like Kyle Hamilton and McKinney, I have to question how much of an impact the previous coaching staff had. There were multiple instances on tape in 2025 of players who were slow to react to the offense, as well as seemingly out of position or unsure of their assignments. What we call “Game Speed” is often the effects of quick processing and anticipation, as opposed to pure athleticism. With that in mind, getting Nubin to take the next step in his development will likely mean making sure he’s comfortable in the scheme and confident in his ability to execute his assignment. Improving his “mental footwork” will go a long way toward compensating for his pedestrian athleticism. It will fall to Dennard Wilson and Donald D’Alesio to help Nubin become comfortable enough in the scheme to play fast. Nubin has said that his role in Dennard Wilson’s defense is more akin to how he played in college. That is, hopefully, a good start for him. For his part, D’Alesio said earlier in the offseason that Nubin’s confidence has been returning after dropping last year. CB Dru Phillips Phillips is a difference maker. Every NFL defense is looking for a Dru Phillips — a reliable overhang player who can cover, blitz, and be a force in run defense. Phillips understands how to avoid and deconstruct blocks. He’s instinctual with elite closing burst. Phillips came away with his first interception of the year against Joe Flacco and the Colts. He has 67 tackles, two forced fumbles, a sack, and one pass defensed through 13 contests. His statistics don’t necessarily reflect a home-run pick, but the level of impactful plays coupled with the run/pass competance makes me love this selection in the third round. Was his rookie year perfect? No, but Phillips has a bright future as a Giant and his skills transcend coordinators. Grade: A+ Mid-season Grade: A+ Like pretty much everyone else on the Giants’ defense, Phillips took a step back in the first part of the 2025 season. That said, he was one of the defenders to regain that step under Charlie Bullen in the second half of the year. As with Deonte Banks, it’s fair to wonder just how much Phillips was impacted by losing Jerome Henderson after the 2024 season. Henderson is a fiery coach and that may have resonated with an edgy tone-setter like Phillips. The fact that he played better with a more aggressive play caller suggests that he could get right back on…

title: 5 ‘things I think’ on the eve of NY Giants training camp
summary: New York Giants players report for training camp on Tuesday, with practice starting on Wednesday. Here are some of the things I am thinking about as a new season of Giants football, the first with 18-year veteran head coach John Harbaugh at the wheel, dawns. That Harbaugh speech The John Harbaugh “This is the New […]
full_text: John Harbaugh | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images New York Giants players report for training camp on Tuesday, with practice starting on Wednesday. Here are some of the things I am thinking about as a new season of Giants football, the first with 18-year veteran head coach John Harbaugh at the wheel, dawns. That Harbaugh speech The John Harbaugh “This is the New York Giants” speech to his team on their first day together has drawn criticism . I think that criticism is stupid and misguided. The Giants are one of the league’s iconic original franchises. They have won eight championships — four Super Bowls and four titles in the pre-Super Bowl era. Harbaugh was reminding players of what the franchise has been, of the legacy they should embrace and strive to emulate. He wasn’t simply blowing rah-rah smoke. Players and assistant coaches have all lauded Harbaugh’s daily messages to the team. To take one small snippet, without hearing the rest of Harbaugh’s message, and twist it into something “cringey” or to be made fun of is nonsense. “The New York Giants. The New York Giants! This is the New York Giants sitting in this room! The New York Giants” Starting to think John Harbaugh is pumped to be on the Giants pic.twitter.com/IJoTmK7dor — Barstool Sports (@barstoolsports) July 22, 2026 Handling a Harbaugh camp I am extremely curious to see how much of a shock Harbaugh’s training camp, which promises more physicality and less coddling than many NFL players have become accustomed to, is to the players. Media, too. It certainly promises to be interesting. Tight end Isaiah Likely was with Harbaugh for the past four years with the Baltimore Ravens. He says he has been “institutionalized”. “With Coach Harbs, this is all I ever know,” Likely said. “Whatever he’s doing at practice, I’ve been doing it for the last four years in a row. So, whatever you all see out there is what you’re going to get every time.” We saw some indications of Harbaugh’s ways in the spring. Draft picks took snaps during rookie mini-camp, something Giants’ draft picks had not done in several years. Spring practices ran as long as the Collective Bargaining Agreement would allow. The Giants did 9-on-7 run drills without pads, an unusual sight. First- and second-team players took more reps than we have become accustomed to seeing. The West Virginia schedule is an indication things will be different. The Giants will practice for four days, take Sunday off, then practice six consecutive days. I can’t remember the last time a Giants team did that. And I’m not Dan Duggan of The Athletic, who probably has that detail tucked away in a years-old notebook somewhere. Position battles We probably already know about 75% of the 53-man roster , maybe a little more than that. There are competitions for both roster spots and playing time that will be worth watching. Here are the five battles I think I am most interested: CB2 — Will the starting cornerback opposite Paulson Adebo be behind door Number 1 (Greg Newsome), Door No. 2 (Colton Hood), or Door No. 3 (Deonte Banks)? Defensive line — If you know who, out of Zacch Pickens, Sam Roberts, Josh Futou, Bobby Jamison-Travis, Leki Fotu, Ben Barten, and Anquin Barnes Jr. is going to make the roster, you are smarter than I am. Wide receiver — Can Odell Beckham make the roster? If he can’t, who does? Is this finally the end of the line for Jalin Hyatt? Offensive line — Who will the Giants keep as their backups? Would they dare try to pass J.C. Davis through waivers and get him to the practice squad? Can Evan Neal somehow earn a spot? Will Jon Runyan face real competition for the left guard job? Safety — This is not really about roster spots. I want to know if either Ar’Darius Washington or Jason Pinnock can take Tyler Nubin’s starting job. Malik Nabers’ progress Nabers, coming back from a pair of surgeries to fix a torn ACL, will avoid the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list at the beginning of camp. How much he does each day, and how he looks while doing it, is going to become a daily story. I would suspect a slow ramp-up for Nabers designed to, hopefully, get him to full speed for Week 1 against the Dallas Cowboys. I would expect Nabers to do more than warm-up drills and perhaps some individual drills early in camp. Perhaps some 7-on-7 and 1-on-1 work as camp moves along, and some 11-on-11 action later in camp. I’d guess there is no chance Nabers plays in a preseason game. A long way from home Truthfully, as I have thought about this column over the past several days, and tried to chisel out time to write it, I have been distracted by my own thoughts about and preparations for spending the next two weeks in West Virginia. I report to West Virginia for camp on Monday, and have been pre-occupied for days with thoughts of what I needed to do before leaving, and all of the things I needed to bring. I’ve resigned myself to having a couple of “oh, s—-, I didn’t bring such and such” with me moments. It is a 586-mile drive from my home to my accommodations for 12 nights. I am grateful for the opportunity to cover this important stretch for the Giants in person — I have always believed seeing things with my own eyes is the only way to do this job corectly. Still, this will be the longest stretch of time ever spent away from my bride of 41 years (as of Aug. 10). I might miss the birth of our fourth grandchild, unless the little man cooperates and waits for grandpa to get home. I would, though, feel like I wasn’t doing my job properly if I wasn’t there. I hope you enjoy, and benfit from, the coverage here at Big Blue View of the West Virginia chapter of the upcoming season. Let the adventure begin!

summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are your headlines for Monday, as we gear up for the beginning of training camp on Wednesday. Dennard Wilson opens up on how Giants’ defense can be ferocious again: ‘Mission over men’ | New York Post Here is a Wilson quote on what makes a great leader from […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are your headlines for Monday, as we gear up for the beginning of training camp on Wednesday. Dennard Wilson opens up on how Giants’ defense can be ferocious again: ‘Mission over men’ | New York Post Here is a Wilson quote on what makes a great leader from his Q&A with Steve Serby : He understands, or she understands, that there’s going to be bumps in the road. If you don’t have a clear direction, you’re going to sink the ship. Every day isn’t going to be perfect. A true leader can do three things: He can teach, motivate and inspire. It’s a simple place to be, you know. “That bonding opportunity … guys aren’t going home. They’re going to be with each other into the evening, stuff like that, go to dinner together. I think it’s a real plus for us. I’m excited about it.” How important Malik Nabers is The following WRs have hit or cleared the 98th percentile in success rate vs. press coverage while taking fewer than 30% of their sampled snaps from the slot in #ReceptionPerception history (2014 to current): – A.J. Brown – Davante Adams – Ja’Marr Chase – Justin Jefferson… pic.twitter.com/rqnlQeigXq — Matt Harmon (@MattHarmon_BYB) July 24, 2026 Leaning on experience with Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes, Giants leaders aren’t just telling Jaxson Dart to run more carefully. They’re showing him | Yahoo Sports … as new Giants staffers settled in, Nagy queued up clips to remind Dart that visits to the blue tent — in the preseason, in his first start and repeatedly through the season — compromise his availability. title: Makai Lemon is a versatile player
summary: Former Eagles undrafted free agent Reed Blankenship earned a huge new contract with the Houston Texans this offseason, and he and Cooper DeJean welcomed Blankenship’s new teammate Calen Bullock on their Exciting Mics podcast. Bullock overlapped with Makai Lemon for one year at USC and he recalled when the Eagles’ rookie wide receiver actually played […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JULY 18: Philadelphia Eagles first round draft pick, wide receiver Makai Lemon, throws out a first pitch before a game between the Philadelphia Phillies and New York Mets at Citizens Bank Park on July 18, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images Former Eagles undrafted free agent Reed Blankenship earned a huge new contract with the Houston Texans this offseason, and he and Cooper DeJean welcomed Blankenship’s new teammate Calen Bullock on their Exciting Mics podcast . Bullock overlapped with Makai Lemon for one year at USC and he recalled when the Eagles’ rookie wide receiver actually played in games at cornerback. Bullock explained that a lot of their corners were hurt that season, and Lemon played both receiver and corner in high school, so they had to call him over to play on defense. The WR took 18 defensive snaps (per Pro Football Focus) his rookie season in 2023, but eventually made his way back to the offensive side of the ball. Makai Lemon played CB at USC?! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/Hp1KCGf2wB — Exciting Mics (@excitingmics) July 23, 2026 Bullock went on to credit Lemon’s work ethic and said that the WR is a dog ever since his early days in college. They didn’t get many opportunities to go against each other in practice because Lemon was dealing with some injuries in the year they overlapped, but Bullock was excited to see how Lemon grew and developed every year. As for the rookie receiver’s personality, Bullock said Lemon is a really chill guy, and once he’s comfortable, he’s really funny.

title: Eagles schedule preview: Seahawks
summary: When and where: Week 15 at home at 5pm on Saturday Key additions: None Key subtractions: OC Klint Kubiak, RB Kenneth Walker, S Coby Brant, EDGE Boye Mafe, CB Tariq Woolen Last season: They won the Super Bowl. Pretty good season. The question for this team: How hard will the return to Earth be? It’s […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - FEBRUARY 11: Sam Darnold #14 of the Seattle Seahawks raises the Lombardi Trophy during the Seattle Seahawks Super Bowl LX victory celebration and parade at Lumen Field on February 11, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images When and where: Week 15 at home at 5pm on Saturday Key additions: None Key subtractions: OC Klint Kubiak, RB Kenneth Walker, S Coby Brant, EDGE Boye Mafe, CB Tariq Woolen Last season: They won the Super Bowl. Pretty good season. The question for this team: How hard will the return to Earth be? It’s really hard to repeat as Super Bowl champions. Seattle is a well run team and knows this. They probably also know it’s going to be really hard for them to repeat because they took a small beating this offseason, losing two starters in the secondary, their top running back, and their offensive play caller. Those must be painful losses for a defensive coach who has a RUN THE DAMN BALL hat. New OC Brian Fleury is a former RB and TE coach, so at least there should be plenty of running of the damn ball. But their RBs are a guy coming off an ACL tear in January and a rookie who was a backup in college. To replace their losses, the Seahawks signed or traded for…. no one of consequence. The 2025 Seahawks were a very good team, but they weren’t “we can withstand this level of attrition” good. In their favor for 2026 is that Sam Darnold probably won’t lead the league in turnovers again, right? Right? Maybe not. Darnold’s interception percentage of 2.9% in 2025 was closer to his Jets tenure, where 2.9% was his career best there, than his time as a journeyman, with marks of 3.2, 2,1, 2.2, and 2.2 again with the Panthers, 49ers, and Vikings. Darnold will likely cut down on fumbles, where he led the league with 11, but he might throw a few more interceptions. Seattle has gotten him no help. Throughout the 2025 season the Seahawks lacked a decent WR2 behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and they still don’t have one. Rashid Shaheed had just 188 yards in 9 games with Seattle, and his career bests are 59 catches (in 18 games in 2025) and 719 yards (in 2023). Zach Charbonnet, career high 209 touches in 2025 before tearing his ACL, or Jadarian Price, who had 295 career touches in three seasons at Notre Dame behind Jeremiyah Love, are question marks. The Seahawks had the third healthiest team in 2025 , behind only the Eagles and Patriots in Adjusted Games Lost. Even just an above average season will test their already weakened depth. Seattle’s scoring improved by over 6 points per game from 2024 to 2025, going from 18th to 3rd. That’s almost certainly coming back down, and that alone could have them in 3rd place in the NFC West and on the road to start the playoffs. If they even make them. 7 of the past 20 Super Bowl teams did not make the playoffs the following year. It’s really hard to make it back to the Super Bowl.

title: Eagles News: Philadelphia’s biggest question entering training camp
summary: Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … The Biggest Question for Every NFL Team as Training Camps Begin – The RingerPhiladelphia Eagles — How will Jalen Hurts play in a new offensive scheme? Even after trading away receiver A.J. Brown, Philadelphia still has one of the league’s best rosters, along with a […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JUNE 2: Offensive coordinator Sean Mannion and Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles look on during OTA offseason workouts at Jefferson Health Training Complex on June 2, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … The Biggest Question for Every NFL Team as Training Camps Begin – The Ringer Philadelphia Eagles — How will Jalen Hurts play in a new offensive scheme? Even after trading away receiver A.J. Brown, Philadelphia still has one of the league’s best rosters, along with a quarterback-friendly environment for Jalen Hurts. The Eagles offense will look different in 2026 under new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, who has previously coached under Sean McVay and Matt LaFleur. Expect more run plays from under center and a more consistent play-action passing game. Ideally, Hurts will be trusted to work through his progressions and throw into the middle of the field. The pressure is on for Hurts to have his best year yet. That starts in training camp, where we’ll get the first legitimate look at how he is able to handle the new scheme. Jalen Hurts: ‘It will be a fun Training Camp’ – PhiladelphiaEagles.com “It carries over. I’ve played with (Smith) since I was 17, 18 years old, so that’s something to consider when you think about chemistry and the foundation of where we come from,” Hurts said. “Having his presence has always been very valuable, I’ve always appreciated that and I think as he leads and as I lead, it’s just about putting those things together and continuing to improve given all the change that we have in front of us.” For Hurts, comfort comes with repetition. There has been a lot of work this offseason in implementing the new offensive scheme in the film room and meetings. While players were able to get their first taste of the system during OTAs and minicamp, the real test will come in Training Camp. “Thought it was a really good spring, being able to onboard another new system and put everything together, lay the foundation,” Hurts said. “I’m encouraged by the work that we were able to put in. We’ve got a fun summer ahead of us, and it’ll be a fun training camp.” As a passer only, Jalen Hurts’ rankings make some sense – BGN Jalen Hurts is one of the most perplexingly great players in the NFL and, perhaps, Eagles history. He has won a Super Bowl, played in two of them, and was the best player on the field in both. He is 56-22 in the regular season as a starter. He has been to three Pro Bowls and was MVP runner-up in 2022. And yet, the football world, including all of us in Philadelphia, don’t quite seem to able to put our finger on just how good he is. 30 things I’ll be watching at 2026 Eagles training camp – PhillyVoice 2) Is there actually a camp battle for the QB2 spot? Tanner McKee has quietly gone about his business as a backup quarterback for the Eagles for three full years, diligently preparing as if he’s the starter. And when he has gotten his opportunities — with the exception of one game last season during which he played with the second-team offensive line and backups at the skill positions — he has mostly looked the part of a player who could earn a starting job at some point, even if with another team. And yet, despite his continued progression as a pro quarterback, he was competing for the QB2 job this spring with a 38-year-old Andy Dalton, who the team acquired via a mere seventh-round pick this offseason. Weird. McKee pretty clearly outplayed Dalton during the spring, at least during the media-attended practices, but it’s interesting that the team felt that he should have to earn the QB2 spot, which in my opinion, he already has the last three-plus years. Eagles Notebook – Nick the Bum – Iggles Blitz DeVonta Smith is poised to have a big year for the Eagles. He’s been really good over the first five years of his career, averaging 82-1067-7. And that was sharing the ball with a workhorse like AJ Brown. Smitty should be a star this season. We know he can get the job done on deep balls. It should be fun to see Smith handle the role of featured receiver. He did that in college and won the Heisman Trophy. He can be a star. One thought on each Eagles defensive player ahead of training camp – The Athletic Jalen Carter, DT: A simmering story entering training camp is Carter’s contract status. Are the Eagles ready to make Carter one of the highest-paid defensive players in the NFL? The talent and the upside warrant it. Carter can be the Defensive Player of the Year, but the Eagles would need to pay accordingly. Betting on the Philadelphia Eagles in 2026: Upside remains after slow finish to 2025 – ESPN 2026 outlook: Upside is still there for Super Bowl LIX winners. We don’t know exactly what we’ll see on offense in Philadelphia, with Mannion in at offensive coordinator after serving as the quarterbacks coach for the Packers in 2025, A.J. Brown gone and Hurts and Saquon Barkley coming off down years. But those unknowns are why the Eagles can present betting opportunities — good or bad. Largely, I’m backing Philadelphia across the board. The roster is still loaded — CB Riq Woolen and LB Jonathan Greenard were great acquisitions this offseason — so the upside is absolutely there for the Eagles to eclipse posted numbers at the books. 15 Eagles veterans on roster bubble as 2026 training camp nears – NBCSP WR Darius Cooper: Last training camp, Cooper was one of the great stories. The UDFA from Tarleton State impressed all summer to earn a roster spot. Despite a shoulder injury, Cooper still played in 13 games and had 9 catches for 92 yards. But the WR room is a bit crowded this year and Cooper is fighting for a spot. Year 6 For Nick Sirianni: Visiting Where It All Began For Eagles Coach – SI Eagles jerseys in town may be in short supply, but Nick’s parents are always repping their son’s team. “There’s almost never a time when I see Fran and Amy Sirianni that they’re not wearing Eagles gear,” said Salisbury. “…To have somebody local do what Nick is doing, an NFL coach, and not only doing that but winning a Super Bowl is amazing, and I know that, and I know that working here at the school where Nick was a student and an athlete, we couldn’t be prouder of him. …We look forward to hopefully him winning some more Super Bowls. He is doing a great job in Philly.” Winning more Super Bowls might mean beating the region’s beloved Bills at some point. It nearly happened in 2024, the season the Eagles won it all. The Eagles upheld their end of the deal, beating the Washington Commanders 55-23 in the NFC title game. In the AFC title game, held in Buffalo, the Bills fell 32-29 to the Chiefs; otherwise, it would’ve been Eagles-Bills. Leading up to that championship Sunday, Salisbury had a conversation with his wife, Michelle, because there was a chance both teams could win that day and play in Super Bowl 59. “My wife is a big Bills fan, and I remember saying to her, ‘You understand if this happens, I’m rooting for Nick, and I’m rooting for Philly,’” Salisbury recalled. “She said, ‘No way, you can’t do that.’ It was a no-brainer for me.” The skepticism about LeBron James and the Sixers is out of hand – Liberty Ballers Those naysaying the impact that LeBron James will have on the Sixers are coming off as concern trolls. Mack Hollins embracing fierce competition in Patriots’ wide receiver room – Pats Pulpit The competition is especially fierce inside his wide receiver room this year. A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs were added to the top of the depth chart, while Hollins joins Kayshon Boutte, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, and Efton Chism III in competing for snaps behind them. For Hollins, the talent around him is simply more motivation. summary: On the eve of the Pittsburgh Steelers reporting for training camp, we’ve reached the final iteration of our Top 30 Greatest Steelers countdown, concluding with the top 10 players in franchise history. full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NJ - OCTOBER 13: (NEW YORK DAILIES OUT) Troy Polamalu #43 of the Pittsburgh Steelers in action against the New York Jets on October 13, 2013 at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The Steelers defeated the Jets 19-6. (Photo by Jim McIsaac/Getty Images) | Getty Images On the eve of the Pittsburgh Steelers reporting for training camp, we’ve reached the final iteration of our Top 30 Greatest Steelers countdown, concluding with the top 10 players in franchise history. From two quarterbacks who combined to win six Super Bowls, to the Hall of Famers that made the Steel Curtain the most vaunted defense in NFL history, here are the 10 greatest Steelers of all time, as voted on by our panel. Meet the panel Jarrett Bailey, SB Nation Chris Carter, Pittsburgh Post-Gazette Don Chedrick, 93.7 The Fan Dave Dameshek, Meadowlark Media Todd Haley, Former Steelers Offensive Coordinator Tommy Jaggi, FanSided Alan Saunders, Steelers Now Joe Starkey, 93.7 The Fan 10. Mike Webster Career accolades 9-time Pro Bowler 6-time All-Pro 5-time First-Team All-Pro 4-time Super Bowl champion 1970s All-Decade Team 1980s All-Decade Team Pro Football Hall of Fame (1997) Player tribute If you asked 100 people who the greatest center in NFL history is, Mike Webster would be the overwhelming consensus answer. His longevity would be considered rare in today’s game, totaling 17 seasons from 1974-90. He was the anchor of the Steelers’ offensive line that won four Super Bowls and was the final piece of those Super Bowl teams to leave the franchise. He was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1997. – Jarrett Bailey 9. Franco Harris Career stats Rushing yards: 12,120 Rushing touchdowns: 91 Yards per attempt: 4.1 Receptions: 307 Receiving yards: 2,287 Receiving touchdowns: 9 Career accolades 9-time Pro Bowler 3-time All-Pro 4-time Super Bowl champion Super Bowl IX MVP 1977 First-Team All-Pro 1972 Offensive Rookie of the Year 1970s All-Decade Team Pro Football Hall of Fame (1990) Player tribute IF it wasn’t for Franco, the dynasty of the 1970s very likely doesn’t happen – at least not to the extent of four Super Bowls. The Immaculate Reception is the exact moment Pittsburgh went from historic pushover to perennial threats. Two seasons after perhaps the most iconic play in NFL history, the Steelers were raising their first Lombardi Trophy off the strength of Harris’ MVP performance. At the time of his retirement, only Jim Brown had more rushing touchdowns. The Steelers retired his No. 32 jersey in 2022, becoming just the third player in franchise history to earn that honor. – Jarrett Bailey 8. Ben Roethlisberger Career stats Passing yards: 64,088 Passing touchdowns: 418 Passer rating: 93.5 4th-quarter comebacks: 41 Game-winning drives: 53 Career accolades 6-time Pro Bowler 2-time passing yards leader 2-time Super Bowl champion 2004 Offensive Rookie of the Year Player tribute Ben was arguably the most naturally gifted thrower I have ever coached. Arm strength, touch, accuracy, and ability to adjust mid-throw. Great feel within the pocket, tremendous size, excellent athlete. He legitimately could have played multiple sports professionally. The bottom line is if Ben was your quarterback, you had a chance to win every Sunday regardless of who was on the other side. Hall of Fame player without a doubt. – Todd Haley 7. Jack Ham Career accolades 8-time Pro Bowler 6-time All-Pro (All First-Team selections) 4-time Super Bowl champion 1970s All-Decade Team Pro Football Hall of Fame (1988) Player tribute Perhaps the most underrated player in Steelers history, Ham always made an impact, whether it be an interception, forced fumble, fumble recovery, blocked kick, or all of the above. He may not have put the fear of God into opponents like others we will see on the list, but he is perhaps the best all-around linebacker of all time. – Don Chedrick 6. Terry Bradshaw Career stats Passing yards: 27,989 Passing touchdowns: 212 Passer rating: 70.9 4th-quarter comebacks: 15 Game-winning drives: 23 Career accolades 3-time Pro Bowler 1978 All-Pro 1978 NFL MVP 4-time Super Bowl champion 2-time Super Bowl MVP 1970s All-Decade Team Pro Football Hall of Fame (1989) Player tribute Many mocked the intelligence of Bradshaw throughout his playing career and beyond, but he was smart enough to pick defenses apart to the tune of four Super Bowls, two of which he was the game’s MVP. Yes, he threw nearly as many interceptions as touchdowns – so did every other quarterback of that era. He also led the NFL in touchdown passes twice and was the league’s MVP in 1978. Beyond his playing days, he continued to be a big part of our Sundays as part of the Fox NFL Sunday crew, becoming one of the best and most entertaining players-turned broadcasters of all time. He was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1989. – Jarrett Bailey 5. Rod Woodson Career stats Tackles: 1,158 Interceptions: 71 Forced fumbles: 18 4 kick return touchdowns (2 punts, 2 kickoffs) Career accolades 11-time Pro Bowler 7-time All-Pro 6-time First-Team All-Pro 1993 Defensive Player of the Year Super Bowl champion All-time leader in pick-sixes (12) 1990s All-Decade Team Pro Football Hall of Fame (2009) Player tribute While Woodson’s Steelers didn’t win a ring in Pittsburgh, he helped usher in the era of dominant Steelers defenses of the 1990s. He was one of the game’s top players immediately, earning First-Team All-Pro honors as a rookie in 1989, and was the heartbeat of Pittsburgh during his 10 seasons with the franchise. He is the NFL’s all-time leader in pick-sixes, and his 71 interceptions ranks third all-time. – Jarrett Bailey 4. Mel Blount Career accolades 5-time Pro Bowler 4-time All-Pro 2-time First-Team All-Pro 4-time Super Bowl champion 1975 Defensive Player of the Year 1980s All-Decade Team Pro Football Hall of Fame (1989) Player tribute Whenever the NFL changes the rules because of you, you were probably a good player. The league instituted the five-yard rule when it came to contact between receivers and defensive backs because of Blount’s tenacity at the line of scrimmage. Even after the rule was put in place, Blount made three All-Pro teams and helped the Steelers win two additional Super Bowls. His 57 interceptions rank 11th all-time, and he is one of the five best cornerbacks to ever play the game. – Jarrett Bailey 3. Jack Lambert Career accolades 9-time Pro Bowler 7-time All-Pro 6-time First-Team All-Pro 4-time Super Bowl champion 1976 Defensive Player of the Year 1974 Defensive Rookie of the Year 1970s All-Decade Team 1980s All-Decade Team Pro Football Hall of Fame (1990) Player tribute Lambert was the face of the Steelers throughout the 1970s – literally. The snarl and missing teeth created the picture perfect Steelers linebacker. His play backed up his looks, as few players in history hit as hard or had as much of a mean streak as No. 58. – Don Chedrick 2. Troy Polamalu Career stats Tackles: 783 Tackles for loss: 56 Interceptions: 32 Forced fumbles: 14 Career accolades 8-time Pro Bowler 6-time All-Pro 4-time First-Team All-Pro 2-time Super Bowl champion 2010 Defensive Player of the Year 2000s All-Decade Team Pro Football Hall of Fame (2020) Player tribute There is no player in NFL history like Troy Polamalu. His ball hawk ability, closing speed, play recognition, and calculated recklessness set him apart from all of his peers. Polamalu wasn’t just a safety, he was a football player. Diving over the line of scrimmage after timing snap counts just right, making the most unbelievable of interceptions while laying out for the ball, and delivering some of the hardest hits of the 2000s made Polamalu the most feared defensive back of his era. He is a true one-of-one player, which is so incredibly rare when it comes to professional sports. – Jarrett Bailey 1. full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - NOVEMBER 10: ESPN commentator Ryan Clark looks on prior to the game between the Green Bay Packers and the Philadelphia Eagles at Lambeau Field on November 10, 2025 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images In its latest round of layoffs, ESPN let go of several long-time on-air talents. One of the more notable names on that list was NFL analyst and former Pittsburgh Steelers safety Ryan Clark, who had been with the network since 2015. The news drew criticism aimed at ESPN due to Clark finding out about his firing while he was still on air. The Super Bowl champion released a statement on X showing support for his fellow colleagues. “Sending prayers and love to all those laid off today by ESPN,” Clark writes . “So many of you have poured your life into that company, & I know how you’re feeling right now. My hope is as this door closes another opens for you all. God bless!” Now, Clark is taking a different-sounding approach as it pertains to discussing his former employer. On the latest episode of The Pivot , he calls the decision to fire him one that resembles a dictatorship. “This was a dictatorship,” Clark said. “A person or a group of persons – a very small group – they didn’t poll the majority. They didn’t ask that question.” Clark continued saying that whomever made the call to fire him made the decision out of personal dislike towards him. “Even though you told me just how important he was, I don’t care,'” Clark said in terms of the mindset of those who fired him. “I don’t care. I know how important you think he is. You work with him every day. I don’t care how important you think he is. I don’t like him.” What’s next in Clark’s immediate future is unknown, but he will almost certainly land on his feet at another network sooner than later. Let us know what you think in the comments .
